📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6Grand Theft Auto VI.

Sources indicate that if you decide you’d rather sit at home all day and play a pretentious, cerebral puzzle game instead of go on heists, Tenebrae Lux is waiting for Jason and Lucia on their JoyStation in GTA VI. While on the surface it looks like just a funny gag poking at auteur culture (and one developer in particular), Tenebrae Lux is a surprisingly solid, short puzzle game that (if you’re not using this guide) may take you a few hours to get through.

But I’m assuming you’re here because you either want to beat it quickly, or you’ve gotten so stuck (as I did) on a few of the puzzles that you’re desperate for help. I get you. Here’s as simple a walkthrough as I could manage for Tenebrae Lux:.

You’ll start out on the shoreline. You can’t do much: just walk around and examine objects. To start with, you’re going to want to head to the left side of the shore (assuming you’re facing the shore from the beach you start on) where there are multiple run-down shacks lit by major bright lights.

Industry observers note that inside these shacks are three puzzles on gridded boards. On those grids, multiple pieces are placed with different 3D shapes atop: three-tiered tall ones, middling spiky ones, and flat ones with a tiny dot in the middle. The flat ones don’t move at all, the middle-sized spiky ones can slide across the board and clear the flat ones if they land next to them, and the three-tiered tall ones and middle-sized ones clear one another in the same fashion. Your goal is to clear all the pieces off the board.

You can do these puzzles in any order. One of them is easy and straightforward, but the other two require a little bit more thinking. You’ll have to use the fact that the flat pieces don’t move and cannot be cleared by the three-tiered pieces to set up the three-tiers so they and the mountain pieces can clear one another once all the flat ones are off the board.

The three main puzzles in this area should be fairly simple to do, though there are a couple of hidden ones you can optionally do that are more difficult. On at least one, you might need to set up your board so you have two three-tier pieces set up with a gap between them that a middle-sized piece can easily get into after clearing a flat one. See below:.

When I move that mountain-shaped piece to the left, it will take out itself and all three of those other tiles with it.

This puzzle will easily make you feel like you’re losing your mind, but I highly recommend trying to work it out for yourself first, if you can.

When you enter the room upstairs in the bunker, you enter a loop that will keep perpetuating each time you go through the door and up the stairs. The room will be almost identical each time you enter it, but for two things. The first will be the calendar, which will show the date as being one of six different dates, and the second will be one of the other objects in the room.

Your goal is to find a six-digit code and enter it into the phone, followed by the # sign, to proceed.

In order to get the code, you need to pay attention to what day it is, and what is different in the room on that date. If you keep going up the stairs over and over, the dates will eventually cycle back through, so if you miss one don’t worry, you can keep going to see it again. The dates are as follows: October 11, 14, 20, 23, 27, and 30. You won’t see the dates in any particular order, but you’ll need to put them in that order when you input the numbers for each date into the phone.

Recent findings suggest that the numbers themselves, you get from finding what’s “different” in the room on a given date, and working out what number the difference corresponds to. There are ten possible differences, and your playthrough won’t have all these objects in the roomâit’s random each time, though consistent within a single playthrough of the puzzle. Here are the ten possible differences:.

Once you get the code right, exit upwards one last time and on you go.

It has been revealed that this one was waaaaay more confusing to me than it needed to be. The goal is to cross the bridge off to the left of the ruins. The bridge has multiple rows of weird symbols on it. You have to walk over the correct symbol in order to proceed. If you walk over the wrong one, a lamp will go out. If you do it wrong three times, you fail and the puzzle resets.

The trick to figuring out the correct symbols is in the ruins and the poem on the plaque just outside.

The ruins will contain the following items, which correspond to the following descriptors in each of the seven lines of the poem:.

The items will be scattered across the ruins. Also in the ruins you will find a bunch of weird, esoteric symbols glowing on the ruined archways above. These symbols correspond to the symbols on the bridge.

Recent findings suggest that to solve this, you need to visit each of the items in the order they appear in the poem, and match the item with the symbol on the ruins that corresponds to it, then follow the symbols across the bridge in order (the direction they’re facing doesn’t matter). It can be a bit tricky to figure out which symbol goes with which item. The best way I can describe it is the symbol for each item is the one that’s over the doorway “entrance” to each item, so the one you have to pass under to reach it.

According to recent reports, here’s a map to show you what I mean. Orange circles are places where the objects can appear, and green triangles are where symbols are. I’ve numbered them, but please don’t mistake the numbers for the correctÂ order of the objects: that’s going to be determined by the poem, and the poem’s order is random.

Also note that #1 below is on the ground, because the arch has collapsed.

It has been revealed that this can still be confusing, so let me walk you through what I got as an example. Here’s my poem:.

First up is moon, which for me was straight ahead through the first door.

According to recent reports, two days of rest says nothing, so we move to the third line, which mentions forests. Here’s the tree:.

Third verse mentions gold, then earth, in order. My trophy was past the mark that had crumbled to the ground, and my earth was at the very start of the puzzle:.

This next line is a bit tricky, as it mentions both sun and moon. But there are only seven lines on the bridge, and the items are only used one time each. So we just focus on sun here. I didn’t get a good picture of my sundial, sorry!

It has been revealed that the last two lines in order mentions fire first, then drinking, which is water. Here’s fire:.

So I’d follow those symbols in order across the bridge. It may help to draw a map on a piece of scrap paper or in a notebook for this one so you don’t have to slowly walk back and forth over and over.

If you fail, the puzzle will fully reset itself, and you’ll have to look at a new version of the poem and ruins and try again.

This bit is a little creepy and again confusing at first, but quite easy once you work it out. All you have to do is walk in the door that’s the furthest away from any of the figures walking through the doors.

In the photo above, the man is walking toward the third door from the right, so I want to go to the farthest door on the left.

As you go, more figures will start to appear. When there are multiple, you want to try and split the distance as best as possible. You also have to avoid any doors that say they’re out of order, so if they have a sign on them, go to the next one furthest away from the man. On the last set of doors, there was no way to get away from the men, so I just walked directly between two of them.

Once you pass through the last door, you’ve officially beaten Tenebrae Lux!

Industry observers note that upgrading your TV's sound doesn't necessarily mean spending a fortune on a full home theater setup, especially with early Black Friday deals bringing substantial discounts on soundbars and audio systems from Sony, Bose, Samsung, and LG. Sony has some of the biggest price cuts, with savings of up to 32% across select Bravia Theater models, including more than $700 off its premium Theater Trio system.

Samsung's Dolby Atmos soundbars are also discounted by as much as $400, while Bose and LG have more affordable options for anyone looking to improve dialogue clarity, add some bass, or enjoy surround sound without a complicated setup. Whether you're shopping for a compact speaker for a bedroom TV or a more immersive system for movie nights, here are the deals worth considering.

For anyone building a premium home theater around a large TV, the Sony Bravia Theater Trio is down to $1,498 from $2,199.99, saving you $701.99, or roughly 32%. Unlike a conventional soundbar, the Trio uses three separate front speakers for the left, center, and right channels, helping spread dialogue and effects across a wider soundstage. You can read PCMag’s “excellent” review for more details.

The Sony Bravia Theater Bar 7 is down to $718 from $869 for anyone who wants a single soundbar under the TV. Its nine speakers include upward- and side-firing drivers that widen the soundstage and give Dolby Atmos some height, but there’s no subwoofer, so the now $898 Bar 7 with a wireless sub bundle (down from $1,099.99) might be the better pick for deeper bass.

According to recent reports, moving down Sony's lineup, the Bravia Theater Bar 6 is $548, down from $699.99, and pairs a 3.1.2-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer and upward-firing speakers for Dolby Atmos height effects. Spending $100 more gets you the Bravia Theater System 6, now $648 from $799.99, which adds rear speakers in a 5.1-channel setup for movies and games where sound moves behind you.

For a more affordable upgrade, the Sony Bravia Theater Bar 5 is down to $278 from $349.99, saving you nearly $72. It's a 3.1-channel system with a dedicated center speaker and wireless subwoofer, so dialogue should come through more clearly while music and movie effects get some additional low-end presence.

Sony’s older systems are discounted too, including the HT-S400 at $258, down from $299, which pairs a 2.1-channel soundbar and wireless subwoofer with S-Force Pro Front Surround to widen the sound for everyday TV, sports, and casual movies. The HT-S40R is arguably the better deal at the same $258, down from $329.99, since it adds two rear speakers for a full 5.1-channel setup, though neither model supports Dolby Atmos.

Recent findings suggest that for smaller rooms or for anyone who mainly wants dialogue to come across more clearly, Bose has two compact soundbars on sale: The newer Bose TV Speaker (2nd Gen) is down to $239 from $299, with an updated acoustic design that Bose says improves clarity and overall sound performance. Meanwhile, the original Bose TV Speaker is $199, down from $279, and offers a similarly compact design with a dedicated dialogue mode and adjustable bass.

Samsung’s HW-Q800H is down to $697.99 from $1,097.99, a $400 cut on a 5.1.2-channel Dolby Atmos soundbar with a wireless subwoofer. Its side- and upward-firing speakers help place effects around and above you, while a dedicated center channel keeps dialogue clear during busy action scenes.

For something that takes up less space, the Samsung HW-S60D is $277.99, down from $399.99, and fits seven speakers, including side-firing drivers, into a compact 5.0-channel soundbar. It also supports Dolby Atmos, Adaptive Sound, and a voice enhancement mode, along with Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, AirPlay, and Chromecast for music streaming. That said, it has no upward-firing speakers or subwoofer, so its height effects and bass won’t match that of the Q800H.

In a recent development, if you're looking for a complete surround sound system without spending several hundred dollars, the LG S6FTR is down to $249.99 from $399.99, saving you $150, or roughly 38%. It's a 5.1-channel home theater package with a soundbar, subwoofer, and dedicated rear speakers. That makes it particularly appealing for action movies and games, where directional sound adds to the experience.

Recent findings suggest that the LG S40TR is another affordable option for anyone who wants rear speakers included in the box. It's currently $199.99, down from $279.99, and offers a 4.1-channel arrangement with a wireless subwoofer and two rear speakers. This should give movie soundtracks a greater sense of direction than a basic soundbar, while the subwoofer handles the lower frequencies that smaller TV speakers often struggle to reproduce.

According to recent reports, at just under $187, the S60T is the least expensive system in this roundup, pairing a 3.1-channel soundbar with a wireless subwoofer for clearer dialogue and fuller sound than your TV’s speakers. That mentioned, it lacks rear speakers and Dolby Atmos height channels, so it’s better suited to someone who wants a simple, affordable upgrade without filling the room with additional hardware.

According to recent reports, in short, yes, Black Friday still offers discounts that can be rare throughout the rest of the year. If there’s something you want to buy, or you’re shopping for gifts, it’s a good time to look for discounts on what you need, especially tech sales, home improvement supplies, and fitness tech. Of course, if you need to save money, the best way to save is not to buy anything.

Industry observers note that follow our Black Friday coverage for the latest and best deals our team finds. Another good tip is to only buy what you need. It sounds simple, but making a list of the things you want before jumping into a sale with millions of products helps you focus and make smarter decisions.

According to recent reports, black Friday used to be bigger for major retailers and more expensive tech and appliances, while Cyber Monday was better for cheaper tech and gave smaller businesses a chance to compete online. Nowadays, though, the distinction is almost meaningless. Every major retailer will offer sales on both days, and the smart move is to know what you want, do your research, or refer to guides like our Black Friday and Cyber Monday coverage that have done all the vetting for you.

Recent findings suggest that the GTA 6 Bowling Alley safe code is rather difficult to find when you undertake the Hit Kingpin Bowling mission in Chapter 2 and rob the place, though you can hit it earlier as just Lucia. This is because the code isn't actually in the bowling alley at all.

First thing's first, the code you want is 0300. Like many other robbery safe codes, this one isn't randomised, and will crack open the safe, netting you about $3,400. Make sure to also steal the unique Gutterland Moreland 850 shotgun from the pool table in the main room.

Now, if you wanted to find the code yourself, it's actually located in Brooks Boatworks, another Kolt & Associates gang hideout in the northwest of Port Gellhorn.

Industry observers note that you actually visit the boatworks with the doctor and Dunk during the Slam Dunk mission. Looking at the map on the wall to also get the safe codes for the La Cascara Motel and Brooks Boatworks itself, the other Kolt & Associate robberies in Port Gellhorn.

These are all pretty lucrative in terms of money and narcotics that you can then sell to Dunk once you unlock his stash box.

#74576. I Thought Rocky And Creed's Major Fight Scene Would Be The End Of I Play Rocky. So What Happened?

I Thought Rocky And Creed's Major Fight Scene Would Be The End Of I Play Rocky. So What Happened?

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (920 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cinemablend

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spoilers for I Play Rocky are ahead!
  • It has been revealed that when I think about the best sports movies, often the big match or game at the center of it comes to mind immediately.
  • It turns out there is a reason why that big match was cut from the film and moved into the credits.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spoilers for I Play Rocky are ahead! You can catch the movie in theaters now.

It has been revealed that when I think about the best sports movies, often the big match or game at the center of it comes to mind immediately. For instance, with Rocky, the titular character’s fight with Apollo Creed is something I instantly picture when the film gets brought up. So, I was surprised to see the fight wasn’t really featured within the story of I Play Rocky, the project on the 2026 movie schedule about the making of Rocky. Instead, it was used during the credits.

It turns out there is a reason why that big match was cut from the film and moved into the credits.

Now, even though they took a “week” to film the fight between Rocky and Creed for this movie, it was eventually cut…kind of. Ultimately, the scene was moved to the credits. So, why did that happen? Well, director Peter Farrelly told me the match was actually supposed to be the end of I Play Rocky. However, a big realization about the stairs scene changed his mind, as he recalled during an interview with CinemaBlend:.

And by the way, it wasn't originally supposed to be over the end credits. It was supposed to be the end of the movie. But when you get in an editing room, as good as the script is, you have to let the movie find its way. And when he goes up the top of those stairs [and raises his arms up], there was such a high watching it that you couldn't get there again.

While the director was very open about this being the right call with me, he also admitted that it took him a while to fully accept that. It took a long time to film the fight, and it’s such an iconic moment from Rocky. However, he eventually came to the conclusion that they had to move it to the credits:.

Industry observers note that like even though we took a lot of time making that fight and doing it, you will never get that high again. You're not going to feel it. And so I indicated it to a few people in the editing room. They go, ‘You should end on the top of the stairs.’ I was like, ‘No, I took a week. I took a week to shoot the fight. I'm not cutting the fight.’ And it took me a couple weeks to finally realize I have to cut the fight. It's got to end on the stairs.

I know I was a bit shocked not to see the fight prominently featured in the movie, when so many of the other scenes are. However, I did think it was a cool surprise to cut it into the credits, and it served as a full-circle moment to the scene where we watch Anthony Ippolito’s Sylvester Stallone and Stephan James’ Carl Weathers train for the fight.

Speaking of Ippolito and James, they, like Stallone and Weathers, trained and learned how to box for this movie. That means they took a few punches too. When I asked the Sly actor about filming the fight between Rocky and Creed, he stated:.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

According to recent reports, we took some real we took some real shots during that. Me and Stephan were just trying to figure it out, and you know, sometimes we messed up here and there, and we tag each other, but it was all right.

James also confirmed that they took some hits while preparing for and filming this movie. He revealed that he and Ippolito trained together as well, and “got close in a very short period of time,” noting that they were “in the trenches with each other.” That became very clear too, as he told me:.

I may have taken a punch or two that I wasn't looking forward to. But you know, had to do what I had to do to pull it off. And I think it was all worth it that we were able to, you know, not only step into these guys psychologically, but physically as well.

Well, considering the amount of time, effort and punches that went into this, I’m happy that Rocky and Creed’s fight did find its way into the movie…even if it wasn’t in the way it was originally intended.

Industry observers note that now, if you’d like to see how this legendary sequence is shown in the credits of the well-reviewed I Play Rocky, you can catch the film in theaters now. And if you’d like to compare their take on the sequence to Rocky’s, you can stream the OG movie with a Paramount+ subscription.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In GTA 6, there are five stores that are locked behind the Ultimate Edition paywall.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, before Grand Theft Auto 6 even launched, there was some controversy online over the announcement of a $100 “Ultimate Edition” version of the game that would include access to a few exclusive shops and in-game cosmetics. So, now that GTA 6 is here and I’ve spent over 150 hours with it, I can share what’s in the Ultimate Edition, how you access this stuff, and if it’s worth upgrading from the standard $80 version of GTA 6. The short version is…eh, probably not.

In GTA 6, there are five stores that are locked behind the Ultimate Edition paywall. These stores include an exclusive tattoo parlor, street clothing shop, and hair salon. Now, at first, I thought it was pretty shitty of Rockstar to hide stores behind a paywall. And to be clear, it still does suck that a few shops are only accessible if you pay $20 more. But after playing GTA 6, I discovered that the world is filled with over 600 stores. There are already so many clothing, car, hair, make-up, and nail options in the base game. So the Ultimate Edition’s extra few stores don’t feel that necessary. And after actually visiting these shops and seeing what they have to offer, I don’t think people are missing out on that much.

According to recent reports, first up, there’s 305, a clothing store specializing in urban, skater-inspired clothing and gear. There’s some alright stuff in here, including some nice-looking jeans for Jason and a cool graphic shirt or two. And a really wild fuzzy hat for Lucia. But the options in here aren’t something you need to have. You can create plenty of great and cool outfits without stopping by this Ultimate Editionâonly retailer.

In a recent development, next up is the tattoo shop Electric Fang. Of all the Ultimate Edition stores, this is the coolest one to enter. And I do think some of Electric Fang’s tat designs are solid. But again, there are so many other options in the game for ink that I’m not sure these are very necessary or worth the $20 upgrade.

It has been revealed that sara’s Unisex Salon might be the best of the bunch as it offers some stylish hairdos for both Jason and Lucia. But on top of that, it offers some really nice makeup options for Lucia and cool nail art, too. I ended up using some of these options during my time as Lucia because I liked them so much. Still, again, there are so many other good options for haircuts and nail art already in GTA 6 that I’m not sure you need to spend $20 more on this version.

There are also two exclusive car mod garages in GTA 6‘s Ultimate Edition. One of them, Rideout Customs, offers some really gaudy and exotic paint and accessories options. If you wanted a neon-pink car with stripes painted to look like cheetah print, well, this is the place for you.

Recent findings suggest that the other mod shop, One-Eyed Willie’s, is more useful. It offers up some really nice off-road options. There aren’t nearly as many off-road modding options in GTA 6 as there are for street cars, so losing out on access to this in the base game is a shame. I also love that One-Eyed Willie’s offers up a random paint job for every car in the game, including non-off-road vehicles, that you can only see once it’s applied. I brought my Banshee into the shop, and it received this pretty pink design that I loved.

The Ultimate Edition also includes some unique free clothing items based on characters from an in-universe cartoon you can watch. These clothes are fine. I guess if you like the show a lot, they might be fun to wear. But…eh.

Beyond the stores and cosmetics, there are some exclusive vehicles you get access to in the Ultimate Edition, but some of these are only available during chapter one for story reasons. The only thing from the Ultimate Edition I used regularly and still use often when I play is the Vapid off-road truck. It’s fast as heck, a great option for driving on the dirt, and can be upgraded into a beast that can hold a lot of stolen loot. There’s also a classic car scavenger hunt side mission hidden behind the paywall, but after 150 hours I’ve barely interacted with that thing.

Answering the massive question of “Is the Ultimate Edition worth it?” is tricky, because it depends entirely on what you value and your taste for fashion and cosmetics. I’ve provided some samples of what’s on offer and how it fits into the larger GTA 6 world.

Industry observers note that my opinion is that if you can afford the extra $20, a few bits of the Ultimate Edition are nice and worth the upgrade. But for the most part, if you just want to play Grand Theft Auto 6 to enjoy the open world and its story, you don’t need this upgrade. You’ll have a great time with the base game and never think to yourself, “Boy, I wish there were 30 more shirts and a few more cars in this!” GTA 6 is already major. Don’t worry about making it a bit bigger.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sarah Michelle Gellar and her husband Freddie Prinze Jr. have more in common than they they bargained for.

In a recent development, speaking to E! News on Friday, November 21, Gellar, 49, revealed the couple recently uncovered a surprising family connection through Ancestry that has them rethinking just how small the world really is.

“We always joke that the closest connection I had to my husband’s side of the family was that for a small time I went to the same high school that my husband’s dad went to, and that was, like, sort of our one thing,” the Buffy the Vampire Slayer alum told the outlet.

She continued, “Then through Ancestry, we found out that our grandparents lived less than two miles away from each other in the Bronx at one point, which they could have potentially known each other. That’s kind of crazy.”.

Recent findings suggest that although Gellar is a New York native, Prinze Jr., 49, was born in Los Angeles and raised in New Mexico. His late father, comedian Freddie Prinze, was originally from New York, making the family connection even more surprising.

The couple first met while filming 1997’s I Know What You Did Last Summer, but their romance wasn’t immediate. Instead, their relationship began with a series of road trips that ultimately sparked a friendship.

Sources indicate that “She didn’t have a driver’s license. She didn’t know how to drive,” Prinze Jr. exclusively told Us in April 2020, recalling how they first connected.

“We were shooting in Southport, North Carolina, which was an hour’s drive from Wilmington, which was the biggest city that was closest to us. … So, I started driving her, and that’s when her and I became friends,” he explained.

The She’s All That actor noted the pair would talk about “life” and their “completely different philosophies on just about everything.”.

Sources indicate that “By the end of the movie, I just wanted to be friends with her because I thought she was too skinny and I wanted to cook for her. Because that’s what my family does,” Prinze Jr. recalled.

According to recent reports, he added, “And so, we started this weekly barbecue thing at her house, and me and my cousins would come over and cook food for her and her friends. And then we’d make sure everybody ate, and that was kind of how our friendship began.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you were having trouble accessing certain services like Microsoft Teams or Outlook, you were not alone. Early Thursday afternoon, many of Microsoft's biggest apps and services were experiencing downtime. According to Downdetector, which tracks user reports of complications with websites and platforms, Microsoft 365, Teams, Copilot, Teams, and OneDrive were all experiencing issues. As of Friday afternoon, Microsoft has restored service to many customers, and has officially apologized for the outages.

When I first published this article on Thursday, I couldn't even load Microsoft 365's status page. (I've reported on many service outages, but I can't recall a time when a service's status page was also down.) Even as of Friday afternoon, the page still says "Service degradation on Microsoft 365 (Business or Enterprise)," and Microsoft says the following services may be affected: Exchange Online, Microsoft 365 admin center, Microsoft 365 apps, Microsoft 365 Apps Admin Center, Microsoft 365 Education, Microsoft Copilot 365, Microsoft Defender for Office 365, Microsoft Defender XDR, Microsoft Fabric, Microsoft Graph, Microsoft Intune, Microsoft Planner, Microsoft Power Apps, Microsoft Purview, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft To Do, Power BI, SharePoint Online, Universal Print, and Windows 365.

Looking specifically at Outlook, Microsoft's email service had hundreds of thousands of user reports Thursday afternoon, signaling a major glitch somewhere in Microsoft's pipeline. The reports did "slow down" throughout the day, but Downdetector still indicated over 50,000 reports coming in every 15 minutes when I checked Thursday afternoon.

While the root cause of the glitch was a mystery throughout Thursday's outage, Microsoft confirmed the problem in an apology on Friday. According to the manufacturer, "This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI [or] agents. The incident was introduced by an issue during an earlier network capacity upgrade that surfaced following a recent network change. We have addressed the underlying issue and continue to restore service to remaining customers and regions.".

Sources indicate that microsoft says it is "deeply sorry" for the disruption to its customers and partners. The organization says the fix rolled out slower than some might expect, since it wanted to restore service gradually to evaluate stability at each stage. It also says it will release a full post-incident report once it completes a review.

Recent findings suggest that during the outage, the company had confirmed that some of its infrastructure was experiencing elevated load, which it stated was likely contributing to the problems. Microsoft then said it was pausing all deployments and moving traffic from affected infrastructure, and that it found that a number of its servers were unexpectedly unavailable after failing health checks. The company then thought a specific component responsible for processing server health may be the reason the system is failing health checks. Microsoft said an alternative service health check method successfully restarted some of the affected servers. The company was then actively restarting and validating affected servers to bring them back to service.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that L’Oréal Paris welcomed its latest Women of Worth honorees with an intimate, elegant gala in Los Angeles on Wednesday night. For the annual celebration, which honors unsung nonprofit leaders, guests gathered at The Ebell of Los Angeles, a venue with a rich history of its own.

It has been revealed that the evening began with an outdoor cocktail hour, where guests enjoyed passed apps and specialty drinks like the “Parisian Refresher” and “Worth It Spritz” under sparkling bistro lights. As honorees and attendees mixed and mingled, they also had the opportunity to pose for a photographer and peruse a beauty bar stocked with L’Oréal Paris-brand lipsticks, lip oils, and glosses, which were available for guests to take home in a plush velvet bag with “I’m Worth It” embroidered on it.

According to recent reports, as the gala officially began inside The Ebell’s picturesque ballroom, longtime brand ambassador Eva Longoria gave the introductory remarks, noting that “this night always gives me goosebumps. I’m always crying.” She saluted her 20-plus-year partnership with the brand and joked that it made her “112 years old,” though she doesn’t look like it, the actor-director noted, “because I use Revitalift.” She gave a shout-out to the many beauty influencers in attendance, including Laura Lee and Desi Perkins. “You guys really changed the game of beauty, and I just applaud you,” she said. “Put me in your TikToks.”.

Sources indicate that L’Oréal Paris USA president Laura Branik followed Longoria, emphasizing the brand’s commitment to and pride in its Women of Worth program, which continues to celebrate “the power of women who know their worth and use it,” she noted. She then welcomed the company’s newest global ambassador, Kristen Bell, to the stage. Bell, who was attending her “first Women of Worth ever,” said she was “very happy to be here” and introduced moving presentations for the first two honorees: Vy Le of WhereWear, which transforms clothing donations into targeted support for women’s and housing-insecure shelters and the people they serve, and Amanda Rice of The Chick Mission, a nonprofit dedicated to ensuring that every young woman newly diagnosed with cancer has the option to preserve her fertility.

Actor and brand ambassador Aja Naomi King was up next, taking note of the room full of glamorous gowns and festive energy. “Everyone highlighted up and showed out,” she stated, “and we appreciate that because these women deserve to be celebrated properly. I had the immense honor of helping select this year’s Women of Worth, and I keep thinking about how much it matters when someone believes in your potential.” King introduced two honorees: Maya Bird-Murphy of Mobile Makers, an award-winning nonprofit that expands access to design education through workshops, community engagement, public installations, and pop-ups, and Christy Vogel of Sounding Joy, a nonprofit dedicated to providing hearing aids to children whose families cannot afford them.

Longoria then returned to present another pair of honorees: Marisa Hamamoto of Infinite Flow Dance, an award-winning disability-led nonprofit and professional dance organization with a mission to reimagine possibilities, one dance at a time, and Chanel Power of Mentor Me Collective, a technical institute transforming how emerging technologists are identified, developed, and positioned to lead.

According to recent reports, during a break in the program, guests enjoyed dinner from a menu that included roast chicken, citrus-soy-and-apple-cider-braised short ribs, and vegan pan-seared “scallops.” Another highlight? The venue’s bathrooms were stocked with more coveted L’Oréal Paris goods like lip oil, mascara, setting spray, and velour puff makeup applicators.

Following the break, ambassador, actor, and model Cara Delevingne led the room in a cheerful group proclamation of “We’re worth it!” before introducing her honorees: Emily Cho of Juvie for STEM (JSTEM), an international nonprofit dedicated to expanding access to high-quality STEM education for justice-involved youth, and Arielle Galinsky of The Legacy Project, Inc. (TLP), a national nonprofit connecting younger and older adults for multigenerational friendship and storytelling.

Legacy L’Oréal Paris ambassador Andie MacDowell had the pleasure of introducing the event’s final honorees. “For 40 years I have been a part of the L’Oréal Paris family,” she said, with the milestone receiving enthusiastic applause from the audience. “After all these years, the thing that stays with me [about the Women of Worth honorees] is the determination to make life better for someone else. That kind of care is powerful.” MacDowell introduced Jordan Pine of Greenlight Operation, a Pennsylvania nonprofit that strives to strategically combat human trafficking and serve sex trafficked women through a continuum of restorative care, and Dr. Christie Brungardt, cofounder of Jana’s Campaign, a Kansas-based nonprofit dedicated to preventing gender and relationship violence through education.

Proud “newbie” Bell returned to the stage to offer closing remarks and thank all the honorees for their tireless efforts to make life better for others. “I will be thinking of all 10 of these stories and the women we met tonight for quite some time,” she said. “Even though their stories couldn’t be more different, they seem to have one thing in common: that they all saw what needed to change and they did it. They didn’t wait for someone else to do something; they stepped forward and they did it themselves. And honestly, I think that’s gonna be my biggest takeaway from my first Women of Worth celebration ever: Never underestimate what one woman can set in motion.”.

Each of the 10 Women of Worth 2026 honorees received a $25,000 grant, mentorship, and national visibility. As the program concluded, honorees, their proud guests, and other attendees continued to soak up the special evening and shared in a few more hugs and photo ops. Before departing for the evening, guests were invited to enjoy a final “sweet moment” in a separate room where a colorful candy bar and glasses of Champagne awaited.

Industry observers note that the Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County, on the 2026 TV schedule, only just debuted as the first spinoff, and immediately had its own drama. Funnily enough, the biggest drama of the season involved O.G. Mormon Wives star Mayci Neeley, who got dragged into the mix when older sister McCall DaPron clashed with some of the new cast members.

Recent findings suggest that things promptly escalated when McCall made Mayci aware of some drama with co-star Bobbi Althoff, resulting in a text to Jen Affleck saying, “I’m gonna f*** them up,” in regard to the individuals who clashed with her sister. And then, Jen told everyone what Mayci mentioned. After it all became public, it was suddenly so much bigger than just venting between sisters, making someone who had previously been thought of as one of the most grounded and level-headed of the original Mormon Wives series come across like a mean girl.

It has been revealed that I’m sure we’ve all said things in a text in the heat of the moment, but Mayci’s words got out for all to see, leading her to realize her mistake in responding in the heat of the moment. She also expressed real regret for having made the statement at all. In a recent apology statement, she said:.

To be honest, I’m embarrassed. I’m genuinely embarrassed that I noted that. I don’t remember the intention behind it because I know I wasn’t trying to get into a street fight, like a physical fight. It’s genuinely embarrassing. I don’t know why the hell I said that.

Even though the text did make me look at Mayci a bit differently from the impression I’d gotten of her on The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives, I also understand wanting to defend a family member and don’t blame her for having a strong reaction to feeling like her sister was being attacked. It all felt a bit middle school, and I’m certainly not making ay excuses for her over-the-top response, but the firsthand experience with some wild drama on her own reality TV series probably led Mayci to have a more heightened reaction than she might otherwise have had.

Anytime you get a group of people together who come from different backgrounds, have them spend long periods of time together, and point cameras at them, you’re bound to get some drama as they get to know each other. It was a bit unusual that this particular drama came from someone not actually in the room where it happened, but it sounds like Mayci has definitely learned a lesson from the fallout. She went on to say:.

It has been revealed that I am very sorry I stated that. I did regret saying that. That is definitely out of character for me. … I’m just going to be accountable for the things that I was upset with myself for. I’ve apologized for it, and moving on.

It has been revealed that largely because of Taylor Frankie Paul, we’ve become accustomed to Mormon Wives being synonymous with drama, especially with the chaos surrounding production of the original series. After the cancellation of her season of The Bachelorette, custody issues with her children, and her revealed departure, it immediately turned attention to the newly introduced spinoff and the drama in the OC. So, I’m glad that Mayci didn’t seem to waste any time in sharing such an honest reaction to her own behavior.

Recent findings suggest that while we don’t yet know the future of this newly introduced series, fellow Mormon Wives star Whitney Leavitt is getting her own reality show. You can check out The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives and its Orange County spinoff with a Hulu subscription while we await news of future seasons, other possible spinoffs, and more headline-making drama.

In a recent development, I’ve played over 150 hours of Grand Theft Auto 6. You might think I’ve seen it all, and that I know everything there is to know about the game. Nope! I’m still discovering latest mechanics, features, and open-world moments after all this time. Sources indicate that first off, let’s start with the whole reason I wanted to write this blog. Did you know that you can swiftly toggle your car radio on and off without having to enter a submenu? Here’s another trick I just learned about: You can double-tap the circle/B button while in a car to cycle the headlights between off, high beams, and low beams.

It has been revealed that I thought you had to hold left on the D-pad to open up the vehicle submenu to turn off the headlights, but nope! And again, this isn’t mentioned in the help menu and if a prompt appeared during the normal course of the game to explain this, I and many others must have missed it.

Here’s another useful thing you can do inside cars: If you double-tap the triangle/Y button while driving, you’ll exit the vehicle without turning off the engine or radio.

GTA 6‘s help menu does call this out and mentions you can do this at speed to have your car drive into something while you roll out the side to safely. But again, I can’t remember a single time when the game forced me to do this or taught me that it was possible. I learned from a random post online. I guess I should have dug through the help menu more, but come on, who is doing that in Grand Theft Auto?

Another feature mentioned in the help menu that I just learned about is the ability to click the right stick in and yell at nearby drivers. Rockstar refers to this as the road rage button, and it’s a good thing to have in a game where NPC drivers, inspired by real Floridian drivers, suck shit and drive like maniacs.

One more useful control trick: You can double-tap the triangle/Y button while driving a boat to get up and walk around the deck while the boat keeps on cruising.

The next time I boot up GTA 6, I’m going to start double-tapping random buttons during different parts of the game to see what other hidden shortcuts and control options Rockstar has buried in this massive game. And if you want some more useful hidden features, check out this blog about how to flip cars and sit anywhere you want in GTA 6.Â.

For comparison, 2013's GTA 5 hit $800 million in revenue in its first 24 hours and $1 billion after its first three days, so GTA 6 is pacing well ahead of those numbers. Sensor Tower had been sharing unofficial sales data for GTA 6 for a long time already, but Take-Two's sales numbers are even higher than the 25 million sales that Sensor Tower reported at launch. GTA 6 is only going to get bigger when it comes to sales as more and more people buy the game. Additionally, GTA 6 is expected to come to PC in 2027, which will be another selling cycle for the game. Beyond this, GTA 6 is expected to add an online mode in 2027 that will no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways for Rockstar to make money off the fanbase. Morrigan from Dragon Age: Origins, with her dark makeup and impossible outfit literally held together with string, seems like an âI can fix herâ romance when actually sheâs a âShe can make me worseâ girl. It has been revealed that the Fenris romance is like a recipe that calls for you to add a little bit of spice, but you accidentally pour the entire bottle of hot sauce into the concoction and then realize thatâs exactly what it needed. 10 Books Like ‘A Court of Thorns and Roses’ You Should Read Next

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Maas’ lush, romance-soaked series A Court of Thorns and Roses has blossomed into a sprawling, complex fantasy series with millions of dedicated fans, and with good reason.
  • The story of a huntress who is kidnapped by a fae prince and brought to the Spring Court as a prisoner, only to become a key player in all that fae drama, ACOTAR is special, but Maas can only write so fast.
  • In a recent development, it’s no shock that one of Sarah J.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that sarah J. Maas’ lush, romance-soaked series A Court of Thorns and Roses has blossomed into a sprawling, complex fantasy series with millions of dedicated fans, and with good reason. A complex heroine who keeps discovering new depths in herself, fascinating supporting characters who shift from antihero to antivillain in unexpected ways, creative and beautifully rendered world-building—the series has it all, while also being unapologetically romantic (and steamy).

The story of a huntress who is kidnapped by a fae prince and brought to the Spring Court as a prisoner, only to become a key player in all that fae drama, ACOTAR is special, but Maas can only write so fast. If you need more books with the same lush feel, here are 10 to get you started.

In a recent development, it’s no shock that one of Sarah J. Maas’ other series would be recommended for fans of A Court of Thorns and Roses, but there’s a specific reason you should jump into her Crescent City series, especially the third book, House of Flame and Shadow. The most recent ACOTAR book, A Court of Splintered Harmony, revealed that the events of House of Flame and Shadow tie directly into the events in Splintered Harmony, particularly with regard to the character of Feyre’s sister, Nesta. In other words, if you read Splintered Harmony and wondered why Nesta was being so weird, there’s a whole other book series you should dig into immediately.

It has been revealed that if Feyre’s grit and determination are your favorite aspect of ACOTAR, Julie Kagawa’s Iron Fey series (starting with The Iron King) will be your next obsession. Meghan Chase has never felt ‘normal’ in her life, and she’s been haunted by her father’s disappearance since she was a child. When her brother also vanishes, she goes on a quest for answers, learns that she’s actually the daughter of a faerie king, and finds herself in a magical world that blurs in elements of Shakespeare’s A Midsummer Night’s Dream. Meghan is determined to save her brother (and herself), but a certain ice-cold fae prince captures her attention, even though he’s as dangerous as he is beautiful.

If you’re looking for some serious romance in your fantasy, Jennifer L. Armentrout’s A Blood and Ash series is a must. Poppy was chosen at birth to be the kingdom’s Maiden, isolated and untouched in order to be ready for her Ascension to ensure the land is protected from the evil force that took her family. But it’s a lonely existence—until Hawke is assigned as her sworn protector. Golden-eyed and beautiful, Hawke offers Poppy the connection she’s craved. When chaos erupts around her, Hawke takes the opportunity to spirit Poppy away. But Hawke has a secret, and Poppy is soon in danger of losing both her heart and the favor of the gods themselves.

If you love how A Court of Thorns and Roses takes the “enemies-to-lovers” trope and builds it into a deep, complex mesh of emotions and plot twists, you’ll love Shelby Mahurin’s Serpent & Dove series. When witch Louise le Blanc flees her coven, she takes shelter in the city of Cesarine, where magic is forbidden, and witches are unceremoniously hunted and burned. Louise’s life gets infinitely more complicated, dangerous, and steamy when she’s trapped into an unwanted marriage with Reid Diggory—who happens to be a huntsman of the Church, charged with tracking down and eliminating witches. And then Louise starts to realize that Reid is actually pretty darn hot.

If you’re looking for a romantasy that’s broadly similar to ACOTAR while being its own thing, read A.K. Mulford’s The Five Crowns of Okrith series, starting with The High Mountain Court. Remy is a red witch, which means she’s in hiding and ready to make a run for it if the fae get near. So when a group of fae shows up at her tavern, she makes for the exit—only to be captured by Prince Hale of the Eastern Court. Instead of striking her down, however, Hale asks Remy for help—he needs to locate two ancient magical artifacts created by red witches, and he needs her red magic to find them. Hale promises to set her free and even reunite her with the red witches still living. More importantly, Remy finds Hale irresistible and has a primal urge to stay with him, no matter what the cost.

Looking for a romantasy with a slightly different vibe from ACOTAR? Variety is the spice of life, after all—and The Fourth Wing delivers. Rebecca Yarros’ Empyrean Series made a huge splash when it debuted, and for good reason—it has everything, from a capable, intelligent heroine thrust into a dangerous scenario (in this case, a dragon rider academy where failure can be deadly) and forced to navigate alliances, conspiracies, and her own heart, which is pushing her towards a romance that might be as dangerous as the dragons themselves.

Love the moral complexity of ACOTAR, where everyone has at least a touch of darkness? Check out The Folk of the Air series by Holly Black. When Jude was a child, the father of her half-sister, the faerie Madoc, murdered her parents and took her back to the Faerie world with him. Raised as part of the gentry, Jude lives in a world where her mortal nature is hated and despised, but she battles for her place at court anyway while struggling with her love-hate relationship with her adoptive father and a growing bond with the titular prince, a relationship that is strictly forbidden. Jude is a fierce and extremely morally gray character, and one that fans of Feyre will adore.

Looking for more smart women at the center of beautifully-rendered fantasy stories? You’ll love Princess Lucero-Elisa de Riqueza of Orovalle, star of this series-starter by Rae Carson. Elisa was chosen for “Service” as a baby, when a godstone was placed in her navel by the gods, signaling that she was destined for greatness. But as a young woman, Elisa is self-hating and miserable. She’s never done anything even remotely great, and spends her time isolated, overweight, and reading military strategy books. One day she’s shocked to discover she’s been married off to the king of a distant land on the brink of war—and suddenly all that rage and book learning becomes invaluable as she struggles to survive an unfamiliar court and help her new homeland survive a dangerous onslaught.

If you loved Feyre’s journey as she discovered unknown reservoirs of power and courage inside herself, you should read Leigh Bardugo’s Grishaverse novels, starting with Shadow and Bone. As a child, Alina was tested by the Grisha and found to possess no magical ability. As an adult, she serves as a cartographer in the army. Charged with guiding the Darkling—the most powerful of the Grisha—across the dangerous and terrifying Shadow Fold, Alina is unexpectedly revealed to have incredible powers and is packed off to train with the Grisha. There, she must determine who her friends and enemies are, even while falling under the spell of the charismatic Darkling.

In a recent development, emilia di Carlo and her sister Vittoria are very different—Emilia is bookish and shy, Vittoria outgoing and brash—but they share a secret: They’re both streghe, and have spent their lives learning to use magic. In this version of Italy, the Malvagi (the seven princes of Hell) haven’t been seen in a long time, but a terrifying accident summons the Prince of Wrath and leaves three witches dead, including Vittoria. Emilia swears to use her power to avenge her sister, but when her revenge is delayed and she’s forced to work with Wrath, unwanted feelings begin to tick up the spice level to an uncomfortable degree.

Industry News: GTA 6 Sets Even More Records

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and, to the surprise of no one, it's putting up some big numbers that speak to the pent-up demand.
  • In a recent development, rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and, to the surprise of no one, it's putting up some big numbers that speak to the pent-up demand.
  • It has been revealed that for starters, the internet service provider Comcast confirmed that November 18--the final day of preloading--was the busiest day in the tech giant's history in terms of demand.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rockstar's Grand Theft Auto 6 has finally arrived, and, to the surprise of no one, it's putting up some big numbers that speak to the pent-up demand. GTA 6 sold more than 30 million copies and hit almost $4 billion on day one, but that's just the start of understanding the impact of the game's release. For starters, the internet service provider Comcast confirmed that November 18--the final day of preloading--was the busiest day in the organization's history in terms of demand. Peak traffic was 31% higher than an average day and a full 9.6% higher that the previous biggest day ever for traffic to Comcast's network. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ble-JJxBBGA GTA 6 also now holds five of the top 10 busiest days of Comcast's network of all time. Going further, Comcast remarked around 24% of all internet traffic on Comcast's network was people downloading or playing GTA 6 on November 18 (no doubt thanks to the New Zealand trick). Additionally, traffic to Twitch on Comcast's network was up by almost 50% and "is still increasing," Comcast said. A spokesperson for Comcast further contextualized the traffic data, telling GameSpot that between when preloading began on November 10 and through November 18, PlayStation and Xbox traffic pushed enough data on the network for one million homes to stream The Odyssey in 4K repeatedly for two days straight. Comcast was among the internet service providers that offered free speed boosts to subscribers to help them download GTA 6 faster. Additionally, Mat Piscatella of Circana shared data that speaks to the enormity of GTA 6's launch on PlayStation and Xbox. For active accounts November 19 in the US, 61% of PS5 accounts "engaged with" GTA 6. On Xbox, 56% of Xbox players globally did. PS5 players averaged 513 minutes of play for GTA 6 on November 19, compared to 494 on Xbox. These daily active user and minutes played figures are "absolutely bonkers," Piscatella said. GTA 6 was No. 1 on November 19, pushing Fortnite down to No. 2 based on these engagement metrics, Circana said. For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Melania Trump has a few tips for her son, Barron Trump, as he navigates his dating life.

Melania, who shares Barron, 20, with her husband, President Donald Trump, recalled the advice she provided her son in the Friday, November 20 episode of her upcoming Prime Video docuseries, MELANIA.

“I always say it’s a dangerous world out there,” Melania, 56, stated in the docuseries, adding, “and be careful.”.

While Melania may have some words of wisdom when it comes to dating, she emphasized that Barron can always turn to her for advice on anything, not just romance.

“I will always be there for him,” she said. “We have very open communication regarding life. I will always be there for him. I am, and I will always be. And he knows that he’s my priority, and he will always be my priority.”.

The former model also joked about her parenting style, declaring, “I’m a very cool mom to Barron, and I remind him all the time.”.

When asked whether Barron has any intentions of following in his father’s political footsteps, Melania stated it was his call.

Industry observers note that “I think it’s very important that he lives the life that he wants and what makes him happy. I don’t like to be controlling over him. He has his own mind, his own character, his own beliefs, and I respect that,” she remarked.

According to recent reports, the First Lady added, “He likes politics. He gave his father incredible advice. He told him how to connect with the young voters, his generation. Told him who he needs to talk to. He introduced him to podcasts, to streamers.”.

During a January appearance on Fox Business’ Mornings With Maria, Melania again noted that her son’s wellbeing was of the utmost importance to her.

“You need to be there for a child nonstop, especially when they need you, especially at that age that Barron is,” she mentioned.

Sebastien Pocognoli has backed Ben Gannon-Doak to find his killer instinct in the final third and establish himself as Scotland’s main man.

The Bournemouth youngster had an up-and-down evening in Friday’s 2-1 Nations League win over North Macedonia, getting into numerous promising positions on the right flank and winning the penalty – dispatched by John McGinn – which decided the game.

But, as has been the case throughout his Scotland career, the 21-year-old’s final ball in key moments left a lot to be desired.

Pocognoli is under no illusions that Gannon-Doak still has plenty to improve on, but insists that it won’t be long before things start to click for the talented youngster.

According to recent reports, ‘As long as he is high on the pitch and is creating one v ones I am happy,’ said the Belgian. ‘With Ben, we know that he is at a young age and needs to work on specific things.

Sources indicate that ‘On Friday, he had great opportunities. We know that he needs to improve on the end product, but he created a penalty and against Slovenia and North Macedonia away he created a number of unbelievable one v ones.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli greets Ben Gannon-Doak as he is substituted at Hampden.

Recent findings suggest that ‘He did that last night as well. We know he can be good if we dominate the game and he can get in good positions if we control the ball. I am happy with his performance.

It has been revealed that ‘He is a young lad, just 21. Okay, he has become more mature than he was, but I believe in one moment he will have a click about decision making.

Industry observers note that ‘I believe if he is playing every game he can make many decisions. He will know that in the next game he will have to do it again.

‘If he knows that he only has to play a game every two weeks, sometimes he can think, “This is my moment”.

‘It is a process. He will become older and at some point will become relaxed in his decision making, but at this very young age what he is producing is very good.

‘I say exactly the same thing to him after training on the pitch. I say, “Ben, this is the next step”. He knows that and it is important he knows that.’.

Scotland conclude their Nations League campaign in Switzerland on Monday knowing that only a victory against the group winners will be enough if they are to have any chance of leapfrogging Slovenia – currently one point better off ahead of their trip to North Macedonia – into second spot.

Pocognoli admits Gannon-Doak's end product has to improve after another frustrating show.

Should that happen, Scotland would have a crack at earning promotion to League A via a play-off in March, and also crucially guarantee their place as a Pot 2 side for the upcoming Euro 2028 qualifying draw.

‘We are still alive in this competition,’ said Pocognoli, who celebrated his first win at Hampden on Friday at the third time of asking. ‘We know we have to do more than this competition. This competition is about trying to build something.

‘But it is nice to have that possibility on Monday to try to create something against one of the top 20 teams in the world.

‘We need to try to be brave. Switzerland have already qualified so let’s go there and be smart because they are a good team.

Industry observers note that ‘It is part of the process to play away against a top team. That is not something we have done yet. The approach will be different and, for me as a coach, it is a game with a lot of responsibility.’.

#74559. ‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Director Francis Lawrence on the Film’s Final Scene

‘The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping’ Director Francis Lawrence on the Film’s Final Scene

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2416 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Vanityfair

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • When Francis Lawrence, the filmmaker behind The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, greets me over Zoom, he’s aware that his darkly lit, gothic backdrop makes him look a bit like the villainous President Snow.
  • Lawrence has helmed almost every film in Lionsgate’s blockbuster series, based on Suzanne Collins’s best-selling novels about a dystopia where a bloodthirsty dictator forces children to fight to the death for the elite’s entertainment.
  • Just as the original Hunger Games film made a star of Oscar winner Jennifer Lawrence (who returns for a scene in the new movie), Sunrise on the Reaping introduces the world to Australian newcomer Joseph Zada.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When Francis Lawrence, the filmmaker behind The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, greets me over Zoom, he’s aware that his darkly lit, gothic backdrop makes him look a bit like the villainous President Snow. “All I need is a big eagle back here,” the white-haired, smartly dressed director jokes.

Lawrence has helmed almost every film in Lionsgate’s blockbuster series, based on Suzanne Collins’s best-selling novels about a dystopia where a bloodthirsty dictator forces children to fight to the death for the elite’s entertainment. He joined the franchise for its 2013 sequel, Catching Fire, and has directed only three non–Hunger Games movies in the decade-plus since. In that time, one could argue, the world has tilted further toward the oppressive future depicted in Collins’s novels—see, for instance, Donald Trump’s Hunger Games–esque Patriot Games. And while Lawrence isn’t naming names, he’s never lost sight of the movies’ larger political message. “I feel really lucky to be able to tell stories that matter, that are wrapped in these commercial packages,” he tells Vanity Fair. “So anytime one of these things comes around, I jump at it.”.

Just as the original Hunger Games film made a star of Oscar winner Jennifer Lawrence (who returns for a scene in the new movie), Sunrise on the Reaping introduces the world to Australian newcomer Joseph Zada. He plays the younger version of Woody Harrelson’s Haymitch Abernathy, a victor of the Hunger Games who later serves as a mentor to actor Lawrence’s Katniss Everdeen. Making a reflective movie prompted director Lawrence to reflect on his own Hollywood trajectory. “The biggest difference is that I’m a lot more relaxed. I was nervous as hell on Catching Fire,” he says. “It was my fourth movie. It was a movie I was inheriting. It was a substantial movie, and it was a massive cast. So I was really intimidated. Now I have much more fun, I will say. I’m much more comfortable with actors, and the amount of actors, and with logistics. And there’s definitely a family that’s built into it, which is very important for me. There’s, what, 14 years of my life spent making these movies? So it has to be fun.”.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Vanity Fair: When did you become aware of Sunrise on the Reaping, and at what point did you and Suzanne Collins start discussing an adaptation?

Francis Lawrence: When we did the original series of movies, and we finished the last Mockingjay, she said she was done, and we thought that was it. Then she surprised me and Nina [Jacobson], the producer, with Ballad, however many years later. And she never tells us when she’s writing. Even when she has something to read, she never tells us what it’s about. She’s very superstitious about it all. So we got the call, which was very exciting. And she said, “Go to my agent’s house. There’s a manuscript. Let’s talk after you read it.”.

I got to his house, sat in his backyard, and there was a manuscript and a copy of Catching Fire sitting on top of it with a few tabs in it. I opened to the tabs and saw that it had the portion where Katniss and Peeta were looking up the Haymitch Games, that sequence from the book. And I was like, Oh, she’s written the Haymitch story, which was very exciting. And that started the process that we always have, which is that I read the manuscript in one sitting, then read it a second time after having a conversation with Suzanne.

According to recent reports, then I fly to Fresh York and meet her at Scholastic, and we sit up in a conference room for about a week going through the book, beat by beat, of what we think the movie is going to be. She and I lay it all out and chat, and she sits on her computer and writes a scriptment. Then that’s the thing that we turn over to the screenwriter.

How have you built that trust with the author of these books, having adapted them for more than a decade now?

In a recent development, that working process happened accidentally when I signed on to do Catching Fire. I had never done a sequel to someone else’s first movie before. And when Lionsgate and the first director, [Gary Ross], parted ways and I got the call, they didn’t have a script, but they had started the process of developing it before I was on board. And so I signed on based on the book and had planned a trip to Latest York to meet with Suzanne.

According to recent reports, the script came on the day that I was traveling to New York. I read it, and it was not the movie that I wanted to make—because I loved the book, and it was not the book. Luckily, nobody else wanted to make that version of the movie either. Our meeting of me just picking her brain turned into, “This script doesn’t work. Let’s go through, page by page, and figure out the version of the movie we want to make.”.

That’s what really formed the bond—just working really, really closely with her. Spending 8 or 10 hours a day for a week or two in a conference room—me riffing on visual ideas and her talking about the story. We think the same way in terms of storytelling, structure, and she seemed to take to my visual ideas.

Sources indicate that there’s this weird dynamic that happens as we get closer to production. We’re usually developing the script pretty much within a week of shooting. But the production is also building. So you have thousands of people working, figuring out locations, traveling in different parts of the world. The stress levels are building.

Suzanne and I have related the relationship to almost like a mother-son relationship. It starts really lovely and creative, but then as we get closer and closer, it’s me being that late teen who’s ready to leave the home, like, Okay, enough’s enough. I’m going to go make the movie now. I have to say, I love the process. It’s not without its stress sometimes, but that’s part of the closeness of it all that I cherish.

How did this film’s futuristic-meets-1970s aesthetic come about?

Sources indicate that there was an element [of the story] that reminded me a bit of Alice in Wonderland, which then made me think of Jefferson Airplane, that song “White Rabbit,” which brought me to the ’60s and ’70s. Then you can look at characters certain ways. Like, Haymitch, you go, Okay, he’s from, like, young Bruce Springsteen, or Lenore Dove [played by Whitney Peak], like a young Stevie Nicks. And you get this hippie vibe. And the Capitol is that Warhol Studio 54 crowd, and Snow like a ’70s Yves Saint Laurent.

How do you go about casting a young Haymitch, finding an actor who can anchor the film like Jennifer Lawrence did in the original Hunger Games film?

Our casting director, Deb Zane, had met him, and I want to say before he did East of Eden. She had a lot of faith in him. We liked his self-tape a lot. But we knew that he was going to have to pull a lot off. He starts as a very optimistic, fun, playful, young guy in love, and in this movie has to turn into somebody that’s much closer to the Haymitch that we’re used to—cynical and a drunk. He’s going to have to go through a lot of emotional trauma, plus have that kind of mischievousness, irreverence, all these different elements that Woody [Harrelson] has naturally. And so we really put him through the ringer. We did a lot of tests, kept bringing him back, bringing him back, bringing him back. He and I were modulating how much Woody we feel in his performance.

It has been revealed that I want to make sure that everybody makes the role their own. That they find the spirit of the character and that it’s not trying to do an imitation of somebody. That’s true of Elle [Fanning] doing Effie, of Ralph [Fiennes] doing Snow, of Jesse [Plemons] doing Plutarch, Kieran [Culkin] as Caesar. Everybody has to figure out how to do it on their own. Then the weird thing is that Kelvin [Harrison Jr., who plays a young Beetee], has worked with Jeffrey [Wright] three times. So he’s fairly close with Jeffrey. When he got the role, he called and mentioned, “You won’t believe this, but I’m actually playing the young version of you.” He could just conjure Jeffrey Wright. His voice, the speech patterns, the timbre of the sound of everything. It was pretty wild.

According to recent reports, were there storylines from the previous films that you felt you could plant Easter eggs for? I’m thinking specifically of the romantic chemistry between Effie and Haymitch.

It has been revealed that there are certain Capitol characters where I give a lot of freedom for improvisation. Effie, Caesar, Drusilla [played by Glenn Close], there’s a lot of room for ad-libs. One of the elements that we definitely played with a bit came from an improvised moment in the [last] Mockingjay. We were shooting this scene in Atlanta outside of Snow’s mansion, which is one of the very last scenes of Katniss in the Capitol. She’s saying goodbye to Effie, and then Haymitch and Effie kiss.

Sources indicate that quite honestly, it was an idea because Woody just wanted to kiss Elizabeth Banks. But everybody thought it would be fun and that the fans would dig it, that Haymitch kissed her. Then it became this big thing of this hidden love that Haymitch and Effie have for one another. And Elle played into that a bit. So there’s, I would say, a hint of flirtation here between the two, less so on Haymitch’s side. His heart is obviously somewhere else in the story. But Elle definitely brought a bit of that to it. That was not scripted. That’s the fun of having great actors.

What was it like to reunite Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson, and Woody Harrelson from the original movies?

According to recent reports, jen and I have stayed close over the years. We’ve done four movies together. Josh, who basically has moved to Spain, I haven’t seen in a long time. Woody I see off and on and text every once in a while. But there was something really special about the three of them being back together.

Recent findings suggest that it’s also really, for the most part, the same crew from 2012, when we started making Catching Fire. It’s the same DP [Jo Willems], the same camera operator [David J. Thompson], the same AD [Christopher Surgent].

Recent findings suggest that [When] they got to the hotel, Jen and Josh were in the bar having a beer or something, and I was like, Okay, I won’t even shower. I won’t get out of my rain gear. I’ll just come in. The next thing you know, there were 40 of us who had been together since Catching Fire, the gang back together. It’s like a high school reunion or something, but in the best possible way.

Sources indicate that there’s a futility to what happens in this film, knowing where we end up in future movies. How do you handle that aspect of history being doomed to repeat itself?

Industry observers note that look, we’re doing a story where you know the lead character is going to make it out. It’s really about how he makes it out, and what he ends up being like at the end of it all. What I’m really pleased about is that the way Suzanne wrote the book, and the way I think we’ve ended the movie, there is a sense of hope that the tragedy is not for nothing. That was really important to me. And one of the beautiful elements in the story, which comes a bit later, is this sense of, everybody has to find their voice. Everybody has to participate.

It has been revealed that it really deals with this thing that I think is happening a lot today, where you find apathy: people not wanting to vote, feeling even if they do vote that it’s not going to matter. This idea that you have to be active, and you can’t expect immediate gratification—that everybody needs to stand up and it may take generations, but you still have to do it.

Outside of my screening on the Upper West Side, there was a group protesting Elon Musk and data centers because the documentary about him was playing at the theater. It was a reminder that there will always be something to rise up against, and always people who will be willing to do it.

It has been revealed that yeah, exactly. And ideally, at some point, if everybody stands up, something will change.

During the 13 years that you’ve worked in this universe, dystopia has felt more and more familiar. How have real-world events influenced your filmmaking?

In the 56 years I’ve been alive, there’s never really been a time where I’ve felt like, Oh wow, everything is great. Nothing is wrong in the world. It always feels like there’s some dystopian sense about the world at any given time. And somehow Suzanne is always able to write these stories about it, which is what makes these movies feel timeless. A lot of people just see them as spectacles, but really they’re about our times very specifically. Almost in a subversive way, I feel like we’ve gotten to smuggle these ideas into these movies that a lot of people go see.

Industry observers note that there are a lot of new Disney movies that have come out this year, but few are as exciting as Walt Disney Animation’s Hexed. It’s also especially exciting when a release like this means a new character has arrived at Disney Parks. So, that got me wondering: could the new magic-focused movie find a home at one of the resorts permanently? With that in mind, I had to field some early ideas from the movie’s directors when CinemaBlend visited Disney's studio in Burbank, California.

Recent findings suggest that before we get to that, it should be noted that Billie from Hexed is now meeting guests at Disneyland starting today, and she will be at Hollywood Studios at Walt Disney World starting Wednesday. Check out a first look at how she looks as a Disney Parks character:.

A post shared by Disney Parks (@disneyparks).

Recent findings suggest that she looks so good! Disney Parks really got all the details right, making it look like she jumped right out of the upcoming movie. It hasn’t been revealed yet where Billie will be stationed, but I think she would fit right into the upcoming Villains Land. She’s not a villain herself, but she’s from a world of witches, and the vibes just seem to fit. When I shared this idea with the directors of Hexed, one half of the team, Jason Hand, said this:.

Villain Land? What about a whole entire land just for Hexe?

OK, now we’re talking! The Hexed trailer indicates off a gorgeous latest land called Hexe where all witches live. In the new animated movie, Billie opens a secret portal to Hexe after accidentally taking off a bracelet she’s worn all her life that has been concealing her powers. Hexe is a whimsical, beautiful land full of lush forests and magic (of course). Just take a look:.

Recent findings suggest that gorgeous, right? I know I’d especially love to see a recreation of the home of Beef Roger, who is a three-eyed cat who lives on the outskirts of Hexe. Here it is:.

I know, I know, perhaps it’s a little too soon to dream up Disney Parks concepts for the movie. It’s not even out yet. But Hexed is getting a ton of positive early reactions for being “unexpected”, and as someone who’s seen the latest from Walt Disney Animation, the studio has definitely created the kind of world I want to visit in real life. Hence, my enthusiasm.

According to recent reports, I love how massive Jason Hand was thinking regarding how Hexed could fit into Disney Parks, because why not? There’s already a ton of really exciting upcoming Disney attractions on the way, from Monstropolis to Piston Peak; who’s to say Hexed couldn’t become the next. When you check out Hexed, in theaters November 25, you can imagine how you’d like to see it show up in Disney Parks.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Shannon Beador shared a poignant post as she remembered her beloved late dog Archie ahead of the holiday season.

Posting via her Instagram on Friday, November 20, the Real Housewives of Orange County star, 62, shared a carousel of photos featuring Archie, who died in May.

Sources indicate that “I’ve been wanting to post about Archie but it has been very difficult for me to put anything together. And as Thanksgiving approaches, it’s important for me to acknowledge how grateful my girls and I are for Archie’s presence in our lives,” Shannon wrote in the post’s lengthy caption..

It has been revealed that she continued, “Archie passed away five days after our finale party was filmed. It happened so quickly. I was grateful that Stella was able to come home from Paris to say her goodbyes.”.

Shannon went on to recall Archie’s final moments before he passed away shortly after his brain cancer diagnosis.

“Archie had been in the hospital and was so drugged, he couldn’t even stand up. We took him off all the medication and he spent his last day doing all of his favorite things,” she divulged. “Archie went to the beach, ate every type of food that he loved, and spent time sitting in the park.”.

In May, Shannon shared the sad news of Archie’s death, which came nine days after the Bravo star announced her pet had been diagnosed with brain cancer.

“Heaven has a latest special angel. Archie passed away yesterday and the girls and I are heartbroken. For the last 10 years, Archie wasn’t just my dog — he was my constant comfort, protector, best friend and truly the real “man” in my life,” she wrote.

Shannon continued: “I have been through so many highs and lows, and through every good time and every heartache, Archie was always by my side and loved me the same way every single day. Never judging me and always giving pure, loyal, and unconditional love.”.

The reality star thanked her followers for their well wishes and added, “There is such a void in our household right now.”.
