  • It has been revealed that sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel users are discovering this week.
  • In a recent development, here's the situation: Following the November enhancement, some people are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, updates are generally good for your devices. The latest Chrome update, for example, patches an actively exploited security vulnerability, while Apple's latest updates stop people from seeing iMessages they shouldn't have access to. In most cases, it's beneficial to update your tech to the latest software version whenever possible.

It has been revealed that sadly, updates aren't all perfect, as Google Pixel users are discovering this week. As reported by Android Authority, Google's November patch apparently shipped with a bug that breaks some Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 cameras. Seeing as Pixels are rather famous for their shooters, this is a decidedly unfortunate glitch.

In a recent development, here's the situation: Following the November enhancement, some people are opening their Pixel Camera apps to find an error that reads, "Something went wrong. Close and open the Camera app again," with a "Learn More" link to, well, learn more. Others aren't receiving the error, but are instead running into a blank Camera viewfinder, as if the lens is totally covered. What's more, some users are reportedly saying that the issue is present on third-party camera apps, not just the Pixel Camera app. That would imply this is an issue with the camera system-wide, not just the Pixel Camera app itself.

In a recent development, to be clear, it doesn't seem like this is a universal concern. It's not like all Pixel users are now running with broken cameras. But based on the forum complaints Android Authority discovered, it seems reasonable to assume that this glitch isn't limited to just a handful of unlucky Pixel owners.

Industry observers note that luckily, there is an apparent workaround here, though it's not totally obvious. Some users are having no luck restarting their Pixels, while others report that a factory reset wasn't enough to restore camera functionality.

According to recent reports, what does appear to work, however, is shutting your Pixel down and waiting five minutes or so. It's not clear why, but giving your Pixel a chance to "breathe" seems to shake the glitch and bring back your camera. As Android Authority reports, that fix comes from "Diamond and Gold product experts" on Google's Support forum.

It has been revealed that if your Pixel's camera is giving you grief following the November update, this workaround is definitely worth a try—especially since more drastic measures don't actually seem to do anything. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We don't know about you, but with the chaos of the holidays coming up, the last thing we want is to waste precious brain cells trying to decide what to watch next. That's where Tom's Guide comes in: We do the work of regularly sifting through the best streaming services and their seemingly endless options of new movies and television demonstrates, and compile an easy, breezy TV guide of what exactly you should be clicking "Play" on a given weekend.

And this weekend is no exception: We've sorted through what's recently arrived on Netflix, HBO Max, Paramount Plus, and more and narrowed things down to a trio of great watches, one for each night of your weekend.

In a recent development, on Friday evening, you can hang out with "The Altruists"; the Netflix true-crime drama centers on the biggest crypto fraud in history. Consider Saturday a pseudo date night with one of the world's most legendary chefs, with the HBO Max premiere of the Anthony Bourdain biopic, "Tony." And a lazy Sunday sounds like the perfect day to catch up with the ladies of "Yellowjackets," as the survival thriller kicks off its fourth and final season this week.

That's a solid weekend of streaming sorted, no? All you have to do is grab some snacks and the remote.

If you love tech-world dramas like "The Dropout," "The Audacity" and "Super Pumped: The Battle for Uber," you'll likely enjoy "The Altruists," a true-crime saga centered on the whirlwind rise and catastrophic collapse of the multi-billion-dollar crypto exchange FTX, which premiered on Netflix on Thursday, November 19.

Starring Anthony Boyle as FTX founder Sam Bankman-Fried and three-time Emmy winner Julia Garner as Caroline Ellison—the CEO of FTX's sister hedge fund Alameda Research and Sam's on-and-off-again girlfriend—the eight-part limited series follows the couple's transformation from ambitious young idealists trying to revolutionize the finance world to culprits in an $8 billion scheme that upended the entire crypto market.

The stacked ensemble cast includes Alex Lawther, Karan Soni, Matt Rife, Madison Hu, Paul Reiser, Jennifer Grey, Robin Weigert and "Heated Rivalry" star Hudson Williams.

Stream "The Altruists" on Netflix now.

If you don't know him for his cooking, then you do for his cool: The late, great Anthony Bourdain was one of the most singular figures to come out of the culinary world, so it's no surprise that he'd be the subject of a high-profile bio-drama.

Sources indicate that but instead of charting Bourdain's days as a hotshot chef in top New York kitchens, this Matt Johnson-directed biopic takes it back to the toque's beginnings as an impulsive 19-year-old (played by "The Holdovers" standout Dominic Sessa) working a summer dishwasher job at a local restaurant in 1970s Provincetown, Massachusetts. Under the tutelage of Chef José Vatel (Antonio Banderas) and the gritty restaurant crew, Tony B. gets his first real taste of the chaos and triumphs of a professional kitchen.

The A24 flick—which also stars Emilia Jones, Leo Woodall, Stavros Halkias, and real-life chef icon Eric Ripert—will make its subscription streaming debut on HBO Max on Saturday, November 20.

The final chapter of "Yellowjackets" is finally here, with the survival drama's fourth season premiering on Paramount+ on Friday, November 20. But if you, like yours truly, are a bit behind on the psychological thriller, a long Sunday catching up with the unhinged antics of Shauna (played by Sophie Nélisse in the past and Melanie Lynskey in the present), Taissa (Jasmin Savoy Brown and Tawny Cypress), Misty (Samantha Hanratty and Christina Ricci) and the rest of the gang sounds like a day well spent.

If you're not familiar, "Yellowjackets" follows a 1996 high school girls' soccer team in the aftermath of a plane crash, which leaves them stranded deep in the remote Canadian wilderness. Their fight for survival descends into a psychological nightmare as the girls begin dabbling in ritualized cannibalism, group hunts, and other cultish mysticism. In a parallel timeline set in the present day, the adult survivors must reckon with those dark secrets and long-held regrets 25 years later.

Stream "Yellowjackets" on Paramount+ now.

Five Hacks Every Apple Watch Series 12 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (797 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The latest Apple Watches have a lot of upcoming features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks.
  • The Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models.
  • You don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The latest Apple Watches have a lot of upcoming features that older watches don't, so I figured it was time for a new list of hacks. While our general Apple Watch and fitness tracking hacks are still golden, Series 12 devices offer new features like native step counting, a Readiness app, an upgraded heart rate sensor, an AI-based version of Siri, and "audio intelligence" that can replay and summarize real-life conversations, within limits. Here's how to get the most out of them.

The Series 12 can finally count steps natively, a task that for some reason is only arriving now, and is restricted to just the newest Apple Watch models. Enjoy it! To add a step counter to your watch face, long-press on the clock screen to edit it, tap on a complication (that’s what Apple calls those little icons and numbers that appear on some watch faces), choose Activity, and then tap Steps.

You don’t need this creepy feature listening in to everything, but it can be nice to have it as a backup on occasion. A button in your Apple Watch’s Control Center can turn the feature on and off. Keep it off except when you have a structured conversation that you’ll want to refer to later. This feature is currently in beta (which you can try now if you want to), but is expected to be available to everyone later this year.

Industry observers note that it's worth turning off the default setting not just because of the creepiness factor, but also because the recaps work best when there is a single subject of conversation, with a clear start and end, and just one context. If you leave recaps running all the time, your doctor’s appointment will get mixed in with your grocery shopping, YouTube watching, and everyday chatter.

Industry observers note that to finish off a recap and make it useful, take a look at the recap shortly after the conversation, tap the three-dots menu, and hit Edit. You’ll be able to adjust the notes and add your own notable details. Siri won’t identify speakers and seems to shy away from including certain details, like people’s names. You can add in what it missed and also create your own bullet points so that everything gets noted down while it’s still fresh in your mind.

This one isn’t specific to the Series 12, but if you haven’t gotten on board with the pinch and wrist flick gestures yet, now is a great time.

Industry observers note that first, the wrist flick: If a notification is on your screen, or you’re otherwise looking at something you’d rather be done with, just flick your wrist away from you and then back toward you, as if there were a crumb on the watch face and you wanted to knock it off. This will bring you back to the watch face and close whatever you were looking at.

The double pinch is another useful one, although Apple calls it double tap. This is confusing because you aren’t double tapping the watch, you’re tapping your thumb and forefinger together while wearing the watch. You don’t need to touch the watch face at all. So, when you get a notification or a call, look at it on your watch, and pinch your thumb and forefinger (of the watch hand) together twice. The watch detects the pinch from subtle movements in your wrist, and it will open the notification. You can then use the wrist flick to close the notification. Performing a double pinch when no notification is on screen will bring up your smart stack. You can then double-pinch to move to the next card in the smart stack, or single-pinch to open that card and see its details.

If you want to learn even more gestures, go into the Watch app, and select Accessibility and then Hand gestures. You can remap a whole-fist “clench” to do the same thing as pressing the digital crown, for example, or to open the control center or Siri.

A little rude, perhaps, but helpful: With the latest AI-based Siri, sometimes answers to questions can be long-winded. If Siri launches into a novel-length response and you’re not interested in hearing all that, just put your palm over the screen. You’ll instantly be transported back to your watch face, and the Siri response will stop.

If you still want to see those longer responses without having Siri read the whole thing to you, you can set this up on your phone, and the settings will carry over to your watch. On your iPhone, go to Settings and tap Siri, then Responses. Select Silent responses instead of Spoken responses. You can then read through her answers, or skim them, as you prefer.

Christmas in July? Why Stop There?

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that why do we let something like the calendar dictate our holidays?
  • Industry observers note that consider it!
  • If the holiday season has wrapped by February 14, the weeks following are the shoulder season.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that why do we let something like the calendar dictate our holidays? The fact that Thanksgiving and Christmas are just four weeks apart means by the time you’ve returned from November family visits, unpacked, shopped, decorated, done the party circuit, bought gifts, and maybe—maybe—worked for a few days, you have to turn around and celebrate again. It’s exhausting and expensive and too warp-speed to feel like that much of a good time. I’m not arguing to ban Christmas—which I am using as a catchall for nondenominational winter holidays, however that looks to you—what I am proposing is, in fact, much more exciting. I think we should switch the dates of Christmas and Valentine’s Day.

Industry observers note that consider it! Instead of condensing so much effort and so much merriment into such a ludicrously small window at the very end of the year with nothing but the bland hell of winter ahead of us, let’s maximize our time by stretching it out. Valentine’s Day is for romance, whether that means watching Bridget Jones’s Diary with friends, eating overpriced meals at candlelit restaurants, making cards, or mainlining chocolates. So on December 24, celebrate platonic love with friends—à la Galentine’s Day, except we should think of a better name—and maybe go on a date on the 25th. If that date goes well: bam! You now have a plus-one to a Upcoming Year’s Eve party and a midnight make out partner.

If the holiday season has wrapped by February 14, the weeks following are the shoulder season. Life is slow. But by the time everyone trickles back home from watching Die Hard in their pajamas or shopping post-Christmas sales or going to the gym, you only have to survive one month until the sweet relief of spring in late March. Nothing makes more sense for how to survive the long nights and cold of winter.

It has been revealed that so we go all-in on spring. Mid-April is when it likely won’t snow again; around then you no longer need heat—at least in New York City—so let’s make that a national holiday celebrating warm weather with seasonal bouquets (tulips, lilacs, peonies), foraged ramps, and maybe specials on dry-cleaning winter coats or sales on shearling boots.

But why stop there? We in America could take a page from France, where May can have four(!) public holidays as a kind of summer practice run. I’d be more than happy to celebrate VE Day in solidarity: Liberté, égalité, holiday! In our version, maybe botanical gardens will be free to the public for picnics. Maybe amusement parks will be gratis? Maybe lobster rolls and strawberry shortcake will be handed out on the street? Can the first summer blockbuster of May be an annual event with free popcorn? This month of long weekends will culminate in Memorial Day barbecues, which is a perfect bookend to summer with Labor Day—no notes.

Recent findings suggest that let’s keep summer luxurious, so summer Fridays will not be at the discretion of employers but mandated by the government for those three months. The Fourth of July can stay where it is with the caveat that if it rains, we get to observe it on the next day forecast for hot dog weather. Nothing crucial happens in August—phone it in, federal holiday or not. Labor Day stays, of course. The week following it in Fresh York is Fashion Week, which runs concurrently with the US Open for tennis—very busy but very social. We’re going to adopt that nationwide as a festive season soft launching the country into fall.

According to recent reports, and finally, let’s turn our attention to that somber stretch of time between early September and Thanksgiving. We don’t get enough time off, so we will move Presidents’ Day from February to mid-October for another much-needed holiday. Then cook a big turkey dinner on Thanksgiving, see your extended family, watch football, whatever, and delight in the fact that you don’t have to do it again until February. But start figuring out your Valentine’s Day dates now—those prix fixe dinners with chocolate lava cakes really book up fast these days.

"Spider-Man: Brand Latest Day" broke box office records, cementing Spidey as a reliable draw at a time when most other superhero movies aren't bringing in the crowds like the used to. Now, Marvel Studios and Sony Pictures have decided to re-release the movie for the holiday season, complete with previously unseen footage that will reintroduce a cut Daredevil crossover. We just got a sneak peek at that same crossover via a picture posted to Claire Temple actor Rosario Dawson's Instagram.

Recent findings suggest that temple originally appeared in Netflix's "Daredevil" series before becoming a mainstay in that small-screen universe. The nurse not only tended to Charlie Cox's Daredevil but also his fellow Defenders: Krysten Ritter's Jessica Jones, Mike Colter's Luke Cage, and Finn Jones' Iron Fist. (Temple didn't appear in Jon Bernthal's "The Punisher" series.) Alas, the Netflix series were all canceled by early 2019. Since then, Cox's Matt Murdock has returned in the Disney+ show "Daredevil: Born Again," in addition to making a brief cameo in 2021's "Spider-Man: No Way Home.".

Recent findings suggest that originally, "Brand New Day" also featured a crossover with the erstwhile Netflix "Daredevil" series. Sadly, a scene that featured Temple was removed from the final cut prior to its debut in July 2026. Now, however, that scene has been reinstated for the extended cut, awkwardly titled "Spider-Man: [Brand New] Brand New Day," which hits theaters on December 4, 2026.

In a recent development, per The Hollywood Reporter, "Spider-Man: [Brand Fresh] Brand New Day" features 10 minutes of extra footage, most of which remains a mystery. One thing we do know, however, is that Rosario Dawson's Claire Temple cameo has been reinstated.

It has been revealed that the actor took to Instagram to post a photo from the scene in question, which shows Temple standing alongside Tom Holland's Spider-Man inside a hospital room. This clearly takes place at the end of the movie, following Spidey's tumultuous final showdown with Sadie Sink's Jean Grey. Beyond that, however, Dawson didn't reveal much about what happens in the footage. "So excited to enjoy this record-breaking movie on the major screen," she wrote in her caption."[...] with an extended cut of new scenes and surprises... Ahhhh!".

Dawson previously revealed how she felt about being cut from "Brand Newly introduced Day," saying that she had a BTS post ready to go about her time on-set that she ultimately had to scrap. Clearly, the actor was disappointed, which isn't surprising considering "Brand New Day" absolutely ruled the box office. Still, as she mentioned at the time (via Variety) "Because everybody's in it, it still means that my character is somewhere in that same universe, and I really love that. So, I hope I get to be Claire again." Now, with her footage being added back into the movie for the re-release, she has even more reason to be hopeful.

Recent findings suggest that with Rosario Dawson's Claire Temple appearing in the "Spider-Man: Brand Latest Day" re-release, the question becomes whether she'll show up again as the Marvel Cinematic Universe enters its next phase. As of now, "Daredevil: Born Again" has been canceled at Disney+, which means the upcoming third season will be its last. Thus far, Claire Temple hasn't appeared in the revival series, but there have been a few oblique references to a friendly nurse. Indeed, "Brand New Day" has made $2.5 billion at the global box office, and the re-release will likely bring in a decent bit of extra profit. The blue hippo balloon was never returned, and even after an offer of $100, nobody came forward, leaving the balloon lost to history.

It has been revealed that to ring in the parade’s substantial birthday, they’ve decided to bring back the blue hippo, but this time, it’ll keep its feet tethered to the ground. Additionally, it will include Tom Jr., which is a new turkey addition to the parade, and Tony Sarg’s Amazing Marionettes, which pays tribute to the original parade puppeteer. There is also a mix of performers to look forward to, including The Voice’s new favorite coach, Queen Latifah.

10 Hacks Every watchOS 27 User Should Know

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1360 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • watchOS 27 introduces a solid set of upgrades to your wrist—assuming your Apple Watch supports it.
  • With watchOS 27, Apple changed what double-pressing the Digital Crown does.
  • It has been revealed that it seems Apple realized the mistake, however, as evidenced by watchOS 27.2.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

watchOS 27 introduces a solid set of upgrades to your wrist—assuming your Apple Watch supports it. While the newest upgrade isn't Apple's most feature-filled, it does include a number of changes that improve the way you exercise, track your health, and locate missing items. That's especially true for anyone with the latest Series 12 or Ultra 4. If your Apple Watch supports watchOS 27, you should know about these 10 hacks:.

With watchOS 27, Apple changed what double-pressing the Digital Crown does. Instead of opening the app switcher, it now triggers Audio Intelligence—if you have an Apple Watch Series 12 or Ultra 4. If you don't have access to those features, the gesture now does nothing.

It has been revealed that it seems Apple realized the mistake, however, as evidenced by watchOS 27.2. When you're using an app while running this latest enhancement, press and hold the bottom part of the watch's screen, and you'll trigger the app switcher. You can now jump to a different app, or close an app that isn't working. Sadly, this only works when you're already in an app, and not when you're on the Home Screen, but it's certainly better than nothing.

While you can load up multiple complications on your Apple Watch, they aren't exactly dynamic. That's why I'm a big fan of the Smart Stack widgets on the Apple Watch, which revision dynamically to show contextual information. Now, with the latest Siri Modular Face, you can access dynamic widgets on the Home Screen. If you've just parked your car, for example, you'll see a widget showing its location; likewise, if you have an upcoming calendar appointment, it will be front and center.

Sources indicate that to use the Siri Modular watch face, tap and hold on the screen, go to the end of the list, tap the Plus button, and find and add the Siri Modular watch face. Once you do, you'll start seeing dynamic widgets when you wake up your watch. Don't expect much personalization from this watch face, however. You can customize the colors and add three small complications, but that's it.

It has been revealed that the double-tap gesture is one of my favorite Apple Watch features. By tapping your thumb and index finger together twice, you can do things like answer a call or reply to a message. In watchOS 27, Apple took the gesture one step forward. You can now use the double-tap gesture to scroll through your widgets; if you perform a single tap, it then opens the highlighted widget or the shortcut. This means you can open and browse the weather app, or start a workout, without ever touching your Apple Watch's screen.

In a recent development, your Apple Watch's fresh Music Recognition app has native Shazam integration. What's more, Shazam will record your request even when you're offline and away from your iPhone. The moment you reconnect, the service will identify the songs, which you can see in the Shazam app on your iPhone or Apple Watch.

Recent findings suggest that it seems like Apple has a library of songs it uses for offline recognition, because in my testing, it was able to recognize a Coldplay song instantly, even when in Airplane mode. To use it, you can either open the Music Recognition app, or you can add the widget for faster access. Scroll up on the Home Screen, go to the bottom of the screen, tap the Edit button, then the Plus button, and add the Music Recognition widget.

Recent findings suggest that apple Watches have traditionally lacked a live step count widget or complication. To find your step count, you had to go to the bottom of the Activity app, or rely on third-party apps. But even still, these apps never demonstrated live data. You’d always have to wait a couple of seconds to see the updated stats.

Now, if you own the latest Apple Watch Series 12 or the Ultra 4, you can add a live step count widget or complication to the Apple Watch face or the Smart Stack. This will show you your precise step count at all times. To use it, go to the bottom of the Smart Stack, tap the Edit button, then tap the Plus button. Here, find and add the fresh Step count widget.

Siri is no longer a voice assistant that you use for one-off tasks. With Siri AI, you can now carry on multiple conversations with context and memory. It's not as robust as ChatGPT or Claude, but you can use Siri AI for brainstorming, researching, and jotting down ideas for later.

The Siri AI app on the iPhone shows all your conversations, and so does the Apple Watch. This means you can continue your Siri AI conversations and view past chats on your Apple Watch. To use it, press the Digital Crown once, then tap the Siri app icon in the center. This will open up all your conversations instead of calling upon Siri. Tap a conversation to continue your chat on the Apple Watch. Of course, anything you do here will be reflected in the Siri app on your iPhone.

Industry observers note that the fresh Find My app on the Apple Watch highlights a single map for finding people, devices, and items. This means you can now locate your family members who are sharing their location with you, as well as AirTags or other Find My items from the watchOS app.

After opening the app, you can use the Digital Crown to zoom in or out of the map. Use touch to pan around. The map doesn't show all items and people at once, though. Tap the Menu button at the bottom-right corner, and then switch between People, Items, or Devices. If you have multiple items, you can scroll through them using the Digital Crown.

Industry observers note that while it's not a Whoop-level feature, the Apple Watch now includes a Readiness score. Instead of individually looking at your training load, sleep score, and vitals, you now have one number that gives you the whole picture.

It has been revealed that the Readiness score ranges from 0 to 10 and is based on your recent fitness activity, sleep data, and background health monitoring. If you have a score of 8 to 10, your Apple Watch thinks you can push yourself, or "go for it," as it claims; if it's below 5, the watch thinks you should consider lighter activity. This feature, though, is only available on Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4. You can use the new Readiness app on your Apple Watch to see this data, but you can also access it on your iPhone in the Fitness app's new Readiness section.

Industry observers note that low Power Mode isn't your only option when it comes to extending the battery life for your Apple Watch. watchOS 27 offers a special Max Extended Workout mode just for long workouts. With it, your Apple Watch disables some features, like splits and alerts, and reduces the frequency of GPS and heart rate readings, in the hopes of extending your battery throughout your entire exercise. To use it, go to the Workout app and select the workout you want. Tap the Goals button in the top-right corner, and choose the Extended option. Then, switch to the Max Extended option and start your workout.

In a recent development, the Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 come with a set of Audio Intelligence features that use the microphones on the Apple Watch, paired with AI models (both local and cloud-based), to identify sounds, music, and record conversation. Thanks to this new feature, one of the iPhone's accessibility features also makes its way to the Apple Watch.

Sound Recognition can alert you when it hears sirens, alarms, doorbells, and more, even when your iPhone isn’t around. To set this up, go to the Settings app on your iPhone and navigate to Accessibility > Sound & Name Recognition > Sound Recognition. Here, enable the sounds you want to monitor, and make sure to turn on the Detect using Apple Watch toggle.

This article contains discussions of addiction.

Don't go to the old reaping site with your buddies and reminisce if you haven't seen "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." Spoilers ahead!

Sources indicate that we've known, for quite some time now, that Jennifer Lawrence's Katniss Everdeen and Josh Hutcherson's Peeta Mellark would return in the highly anticipated major-screen prequel "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping." If you've read the book, you know that they come back for an epilogue, and in late October 2026 — just about a month before the film's release — Lawrence opened up about the experience and confirmed that Woody Harrelson, who plays the older version of "Sunrise's" protagonist Haymitch Abernathy in the original Hunger Games films, is also part of the scene. So ... what happens?

According to recent reports, there are some differences between the epilogue in the book and the film adaptation helmed by Francis Lawrence, but the gist is the same — and I'll return to those differences later on. After we see how Haymitch wins his games and how the Capitol punishes him for attempting to destroy the 50th Games arena — Haymitch attempts to blow up a water tank and essentially drown the machine, but safeguards stop his proposal from going through, and his family and loved ones are killed upon his return to District 12 — we see Harrelson's Haymitch approach an ivy-covered structure that's the old site of the annual reaping that chose one boy and one girl to compete in the deadly Games. He's joined by Katniss and Peeta, who wish him a happy birthday; it's a major plot point in "Sunrise" that reaping day always falls on Haymitch's birthdays. They thank him for everything, and Haymitch claims "Nevermore" before departing.

Putting the prequel "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes" aside — because none of the characters I'm talking about were alive during that story — it makes complete sense for Katniss and Peeta to show up to close out Haymitch's standalone movie. The three are, for all intents and purposes during the original Hunger Games timeline, a package deal. We see, at the end of "Sunrise on the Reaping," that Haymitch arrives home in District 12 and sees the coffins of his fellow tributes, and we also see a montage of Joseph Zada's younger take on the character overseeing the delivery of coffins that are clearly tributes he was forced to mentor as a former victor.

By the time we get to the 74th Games, Haymitch is constantly drunk and imbibes to survive, telling his tributes his only advice is that they stay alive. When he and Katniss click, though, he starts to wonder if these tributes have what it takes ... and thanks to a plot conceived by him and Peeta that presents Katniss and Peeta as star-crossed lovers forced to compete, they get to jointly win the Games.

That next year, only previous victors can be reaped, and Katniss and Peeta go back in to fight, though Haymitch hatches a strategy with other rebels to break them out of the arena. Though Peeta is kidnapped, tortured, and brainwashed by the Capitol, they eventually rescue him and take down the Capitol, ultimately returning to District 12 to live out the rest of their days together.

In "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping," this ending for Haymitch, Katniss, and Peeta feels hopeful and optimistic. Suzanne Collins, the author of the franchise, takes a darker approach in the literary epilogues for both "Mockingjay" and "Sunrise on the Reaping." In "Mockingjay," Katniss notes that both she and Peeta have post-traumatic stress disorder and still suffer greatly, experiencing night terrors and other symptoms. In the book version of "Sunrise," Haymitch speaks directly to the reader about how he didn't even want to care about his two tributes initially because he felt too broken, but he was worn down. "I didn't want to let them in, her and Peeta, but the walls of a person's heart are not impregnable, not if they have ever known love," he muses before mourning his one true love, Lenore Dove Baird (Whitney Peak in the film), who was poisoned by Capitol forces when Haymitch initially returned to District 12 as a victor.

Beyond that, Haymitch is blunt about the way that chronic drinking has affected his body. "I'm not sure I'll be here in the old therebefore much longer. My liver's wrecked and I only dry out when the train's late," he states. "I drink differently these days, though, less to forget, more out of habit. When my time comes, it comes, but I've no idea when that will be." Still, Haymitch gets a relatively happy ending with Katniss and Peeta.

"The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" is in theaters.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • At the age of four, Joshua Bell was given his first violin, and he hasn’t put it down since.
  • Today, the Grammy Award–winning musician is one of the most celebrated classical violinists of his era.
  • That kinship was solidified over coupes of Champagne and hand-dived Orkney scallops, with the hotel celebrating Bell, a “Langham Luminary,” in its London ballroom packed with writers, artists, designers, and musicians.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

At the age of four, Joshua Bell was given his first violin, and he hasn’t put it down since. “I don’t remember falling in love with music,” indicates Bell. “Music has just been my life. I used to string rubber bands on my dresser drawers and make pitches by pulling the drawers out. I was fascinated with strings. It’s the closest instrument to the human voice. And I find it the most expressive instrument.”.

Today, the Grammy Award–winning musician is one of the most celebrated classical violinists of his era. By 14, Bell was performing with the Philadelphia Orchestra, and would soon be touring the world. “I live in hotels 250 days a year,” says Bell of the nonstop schedule he has maintained since his teens. Specifically, Bell has been “staying at the Langham for decades now,” he says, referring to the regal central London hotel that first opened in 1865. “I chose it on my own because it was near one of my favorite halls in London, which is the Wigmore Hall. And now I stay with them whenever I’m traveling.”.

That kinship was solidified over coupes of Champagne and hand-dived Orkney scallops, with the hotel celebrating Bell, a “Langham Luminary,” in its London ballroom packed with writers, artists, designers, and musicians.

Attendees included actor Simon Callow, House of Dragon actor Emily Carey, former British culture minister Ed Vaizey, Saturday Night Live UK cast producer Susie Hall, stage and television actor Indira Varma, and Verity actor Ismael Cruz Córdova.

Sources indicate that held in partnership with Vanity Fair, the evening marked the latest iteration of the Langham’s Luminaries in Residence program. The event series is continuation of the hotel’s legacy that brings together a diverse, influential community—an evocative reminder of prominent guests from its storied past, including Charles Dickens, Winston Churchill, George Orwell, Oscar Wilde, and Mark Twain.

“I’m not going to put my name in the same sentence as Toscanini or Mark Twain—who has stayed here, or Churchill, who has stayed here. But it’s cool to be part of the history,” indicates Bell. “So maybe someday, in a hundred years, there will be a violinist who might say that—that I stayed here. I don’t know, maybe that would mean something.”.

Recent findings suggest that it certainly does mean something. Pierce Brosnan and his wife, Keely Shaye Brosnan, “have been huge fans of Joshua for many, many years,” Brosnan tells me. “Keely went to go see him…I don’t know how many years back. Unfortunately, due to the LA traffic, she got there late, five minutes late, and they wouldn’t let her into the concert. So tonight is one of those nights.”.

Industry observers note that bell, who performed mid-dinner with members of the Academy of St. Martin in the Fields—with a surprise appearance from his wife, soprano Larisa Martínez—brought about a collective catharsis.

Dazzling, fiery, and flamboyant, the experience of watching Bell up close is impossible to replicate. “I just think he’s incredibly soulful, and there’s something really elegant,” actor Russell Tovey tells me, before explaining how he actually discovered Bell via his Instagram algorithm.

Recent findings suggest that for actor Lesley Manville, the event marked her introduction to Bell’s music. “I’m a bit embarrassed that he was not on my radar. But isn’t that nice to have a surprise like that?” indicates Manville. “Schubert’s String Quintet is one of my favorite pieces of music. It’s unbelievably beautiful. You think of a violin, you think of those strings. And it’s instant emotion. They just make you cry.”.

There is a great power in being able to access the emotions of others, as Bell does.

“I think it is the ultimate gift to be able to make people happy,” says Brosnan. “My job is being an entertainer—to take the words of great writing and try to transform it into something that is meaningful and memorable.”.

Speaking of entertaining, the week’s announcement that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond was front of mind. “I wish him every joy and every success. He and I made a movie a number of years ago called Remember Me. I played his father. So I was very, very pleased and joyful for his nomination and now his success, and I believe he will be magnificent.”.

And that creative full circle is exactly what the night was advocating. “Our own Luminaries in Residence program reflects our belief that meaningful hospitality creates genuine connection with extraordinary talents with one another, and with arts,” Bob van den Oord, CEO of Langham Hospitality Group, explained as he took the stage. “The Langham isn’t simply a place to stay, but a place to gather, exchange ideas, and indeed celebrate.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications.
  • The substantial AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe.
  • Recent findings suggest that openAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

AI safety for both adults and children is under greater scrutiny than ever before, with a growing number of questions and concerns appearing around how beneficial or otherwise these conversational bots actually are for our mental well-being—even without considering their energy use, ethics, or economic implications. At the same time, an increasing number of apps and services are becoming age-gated in a growing number of countries around the world, as governments realize that letting kids loose on AI apps, social media platforms, and the web at large might not be the best idea for their ongoing development and prosperity.

The substantial AI apps, such as ChatGPT and Gemini, are right in the center of these trends, and the companies behind them are taking steps that they promise will keep children safe. If you want to know what youngsters in your family may be getting exposed to, and what you can do about it, here's the rundown.

Recent findings suggest that openAI's ChatGPT has one of the more comprehensive setups in terms of parental controls. The minimum age for users is 13, and if you're under 18, you need to have parental consent to open an account—age is predicted via several signals, including what times of day you use ChatGPT and what you talk about.

According to recent reports, accounts for under-18s automatically become ChatGPT for Teens accounts. There's more of a focus on learning and study (with a dedicated study mode), as well as "age-appropriate safeguards to help reduce exposure to sensitive or potentially harmful content." There are built-in protections for "harmful topics," including sexual, romantic, or violent roleplay, graphic violence, and self-harm. These work on top of the safeguards for all customers that limit chats about physical harm and illegal activity.

Recent findings suggest that these ChatGPT for Teens accounts can also be linked to a parental account—but while parental consent is required for under-18s to use the service, ChatGPT clearly indicates that teens do have the option to break the link if they want. If you do persuade your kid to keep your accounts connected, you can set time limits on when the AI bot can be used, and tweak some of the sensitivity settings. However, you can't view any conversations.

To set up parental controls from ChatGPT on the web, click your profile icon (bottom left), then Settings > Parental controls > Add family member and follow the instructions. It's also worth bearing in mind that ChatGPT app can also be used for free, anonymously, in any web browser, though OpenAI indicates owners accessing the AI this way are subject to the default under-18s limits (and can't save chats or access an archive).

Gemini is tied into everything else Google does, and follows the broader rules for Google accounts: No under-13s, unless you're part of a family group and using an account managed by an adult. You can manage your family through the Family Link portal on the web, though as far as parental controls specific to Gemini go, you can only enable or disable access to the AI (settings like screen time apply across all enabled apps).

Recent findings suggest that for all under-18s (partly identified through age estimation), whether or not they're part of a managed family group, Google applies some additional protections. They include preventing the AI from taking on a persona, guarding against emotional dependence on the AI, and discouraging bullying and other forms of harassment. There are also safeguards to limit chats about age-restricted substances like alcohol or vapes, and mental health issues like eating disorders.

Industry observers note that these protections for minors are applied in addition to the usual guardrails in Gemini for everyone. The guardrails should lead you away from conversations about self-harm, suicide, violence, and illegal activities, and offer quick links to support in times of crisis. However, Google itself admits that these filters aren't perfect.

As with ChatGPT, there's a loophole of sorts in that anyone can start chatting with Gemini, for free inside a web browser, with no checks at all. These conversations can't be saved and come up against usage limits fairly quickly, but they're only protected by the general restrictions for all accounts, not the ones specific to minors.

It has been revealed that meta AI will show up in several apps that young people and children are likely to use, including WhatsApp and Instagram, as well as having its own separate app on the web and on phones. The standard restrictions for Meta's social media accounts apply to its AI too: A minimum age of 13, and restrictions for all under-18s. Like many other platforms, it uses some AI magic to flag up accounts being used by minors.

If you're under 18 and on a Meta Teen account, you'll come up against blocks if you try to get Meta AI to engage in sexual or romantic roleplay, or discuss alcohol or substance misuse. Chats on topics such as eating disorders and self-harm will prompt the AI to offer guidance towards relevant support services.

Industry observers note that meta offers a comprehensive parental control setup for its apps, including Meta AI, but connecting a parent account isn't compulsory for teens. This is handled through the Meta Family Center portal, and parents can get reports on the general topics that kids are chatting about with AI—though they don't get the exact transcripts or prompts. Any self-harm or suicide discussion can trigger an alert to the connected parent account.

All users, under 18 or over 18, get support and crisis intervention responses when chatting about suicide and self-harm, and there are strict limits on discussing illegal and harmful acts, including drug use and cyberbullying, as well as sexual and adult content.

Industry observers note that apple users have to be 13 or over to have an account, which is required to access Siri AI—anyone younger needs to have an account created for them by an adult, and these accounts can only get at the basic, older Siri. Date of birth must be declared when opening an Apple account, with tighter checks rolling out in many parts of the world.

It has been revealed that anyone over the age of 13 can have an Apple account and use the Siri AI app, with or without a connected parent account, as it stands in most U.S. states. This means the well-being safeguards are essentially the same for teens as they are for adults: There are safeguards around self-harm, suicide, sexual and violent content, and illegal commands. It's one of the more conservative AIs when it comes to what it will talk about.

The new and improved Siri AI can be managed to some extent by the new parental controls available in iOS 27 and Apple's other software updates for 2026—Apple has clearly seen the way the wind is blowing—but this is optional for teens. It depends on whether or not you can corral your kids into a Family Sharing group.

It has been revealed that if your teens are in your family group of customers, then the standard Screen Time rules apply for controlling app usage limits and device access (in iOS Settings, tap your name, then Family to get at them). There are also options for disabling certain Siri AI features, such as the writing tools or the image creation capabilities.

Sources indicate that like Gemini/Google and Apple/Siri, Copilot is tied into the wider Microsoft ecosystem, and access for under-18s can be managed through it. Users must be 13 or older to hold a Microsoft or a Copilot account—and again, there's some underlying tech in place to detect anyone who might be deliberately lying about their age.

In a recent development, if you've got a teen using Copilot, you can manage their access through the standard Microsoft Family Safety portal. You're able to enable or disable Copilot access, set times during which Copilot can and can't be used, and disable certain features like image generation or voice mode. Parents can't read the Copilot chats of their kids, though.

Parental supervision is optional—a teen aged 13–17 can use Copilot without linking their account to an adult one. Microsoft indicates users identified as under 18 won't see personalized results or ads, and will get age-appropriate responses regarding risky or harmful content, though there's not much detail on what that entails.

More generally, content around self-harm, violence, adult content, harassment, and harmful or illegal activity is banned on the AI platform. Any prompts about suicide or drugs will bring up support options rather than answers, whether you're an adult or a young person using the service.

Ultimately that means that minors have the same access to Grok as adults, if they want it—an AI platform that combines "weak safety guardrails" and "a range of extremely harmful content" that includes "explicit sexual content, mental health risks, violent content, and inappropriate responses to... offensive content" (that's the Common Sense Media Report again).

According to recent reports, yes, this is the AI chatbot that has previously had a problem with deepfake porn imagery, and which has traditionally taken a rather casual attitude towards safety concerns, led by SpaceXAI CEO Elon Musk. While illegal and harmful content is supposedly banned from Grok, its own FAQs admit that certain chats can result in "dialogue that may involve coarse language, crude humor, sexual situations, or violence.".

Recent findings suggest that there is actually a Grok Kids Mode that limits the kind of content that can be shown and the conversation topics that can be added, but it requires consumers to self-declare themselves as minors and is easy to bypass. The advice from Common Sense Media seems to be the way to go with Grok: Do not let your teens access it.

Claude's approach to child safety is straightforward: You can only register for an account if you're over 18. It is possible to lie about your age when signing up, but like the other platforms, Anthropic looks at various "signals" in behavior to spot minors—if your account gets flagged, you have to verify your age using an option like face age estimation or Yoti.

There's no free web access to the chatbot, like there is with ChatGPT and Gemini, so if you're under 18, you're locked out from the service unless you know the behavioral tricks to get past Claude's detection systems.

In terms of more general well-being protections on Claude, any chat around self-harm or suicide will guide users towards helplines and other resources for support. Conversations about illegal activities, disallowed speech, and explicit sexual content are banned from the platform. In recent months, Anthropic says it's also reduced AI sycophancy.

That's something of a whistle-stop tour of the significant seven AI chatbots, but if you're a parent, it should give you some idea of what's out there and how easy it is to access. Besides the parental controls built into these AIs (or not), you also have the settings available at the platform level—Android, iOS, Windows, macOS—to restrict the use of any potentially harmful apps.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Unlike the "Star Wars" saga, the "Hunger Games" franchise has defied the odds to deliver two stellar prequel films set before the events of the very first dystopian sci-fi action movie adapted from author Suzanne Collins' original books.

Sources indicate that after launching in 2012, "The Hunger Games" delivered a four-part massive screen property telling the story of rebellious Katniss Everdeen (Jennifer Lawrence) and an ensemble of revolutionaries attempting to topple the oppressive, wealthy government known as The Capitol. But the franchise has since returned with stories set decades in the past. This started with 2023's "The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes," which offered a rich portrait of a young Coriolanus Snow (Tom Blyth) acting as a mentor to a bold Hunger Games tribute named Lucy Gray Baird (Rachel Zegler).

Industry observers note that now, the story continues 40 years later, with the excellent "Sunrise on the Reaping" focusing on a young Haymitch Abernathy (Woody Harrelson in the previous movies, now played by Joseph Zada in the prequel) as he's forced into the 50th Hunger Games. This event marks the second Quarter Quell, which takes place 24 years before the first installment of the overall franchise.

"Sunrise on the Reaping" (watch the trailer) might be the most brutal, heartbreaking chapter of the "Hunger Games" franchise yet, if only because the fall of Haymitch Abernathy — from charming, kind-hearted District 12 citizen to hopeless, grizzled, bitter, and drunk Hunger Games victor turned tribute mentor — is incredibly heartbreaking.

What happened to Haymitch after the 50th Hunger Games that sent him on a downward spiral? Join us as we explain the ending of "The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping" to break it all down.

Before we explain the ending of "Sunrise on the Reaping," we need to set the stage a bit, so you know how and why Haymitch ends up where he does by the end of the movie.

It has been revealed that haymitch didn't have rebellion burning in his heart as the 50th Hunger Games were beginning, though his girlfriend Lenore (Whitney Peak) put the spark of revolution in his mind, longing for a day when the sun would not rise on another reaping, overshadowing Haymitch's birthday. But Haymitch took it all in stride, even going out of his way to get a little bag of gumdrops for Lenore.

Unfortunately, Haymitch ends up in the 50th Hunger Games while trying to break up an altercation between Lenore and the Capitol police after she tries to let a grieving mother embrace her son, who has just been shot following an attempted escape from his obligation as one of the four District 12 tributes. District 12 tribute escort Drusilla Sickle (Glenn Close), a cruel Capitol citizen, then punishes Haymitch by forcing him to be the replacement tribute, with a little behind-the-scenes editing help from Hunger Games broadcast producer Plutarch Heavensbee (Jesse Plemons, playing a younger version of the character portrayed by the late Philip Seymour Hoffman in the original franchise).

Sources indicate that if that wasn't enough to light the spark of rebellion in Haymitch's heart, the events of the 50th Hunger Games welcome parade for the tributes certainly did the trick. After Capitol citizens throw colorful smoke flares into the Capitol arena where the parade is held, the horses pulling tributes in chariots get startled, creating a chaotic scene that results in the death of Louella McCoy (Molly McCann), a younger girl who admires Haymitch and was drawn as one of his three other fellow tributes.

After the death of Louella, Haymitch wants nothing more than to lash out at the Capitol, and he begins doing so by walking up to President Snow's (Ralph Fiennes) balcony in the parade arena and mockingly applauding him for directly bringing about the death and destruction laying in front of him.

Meanwhile, Haymitch is also joined in the 50th Hunger Games by fellow District 12 tributes Maysilee Donner (Mckenna Grace), a somewhat snobby and sassy 16-year-old girl who has a reputation for being a bit mean. But once forced into the Hunger Games, she softens and allies with Haymitch and the rest of the District 12 tributes. That includes Wyatt Callow (Ben Wang), who comes from a family known as the "Booker Boys," because their family calculates odds and takes bets on the Hunger Games, which many view as a cruel practice. And despite the death of Louella, a Capitol-controlled lookalike replacement girl (Iona Bell) is forced to take her place, and the District 12 tributes take her under their protection.

According to recent reports, wyatt is killed almost as soon as the Hunger Games begin, when the tributes make a wild dash for weapons. But Haymitch, fake-Louella, and Maysilee make it out alive, though the former has chosen to disassociate himself from the rest of the group, having been told directly by President Snow that he will not make it out of the Hunger Games alive, as penance for his mocking defiance at the parade. Haymitch doesn't want anyone else to suffer for his defiance. But little does Snow know that Plutarch Heavensbee, with the help of several other Hunger Games mentors and tributes, are using Haymitch as a vessel for a rebellion meant to stop the games once and for all.

It has been revealed that in the games, Haymitch works with a clever tribute named Ampert Latier (Percy Daggs IV), who is mentored by his father Beetee (the tech-wise character played by Jeffrey Wright in the original films, now played by Kelvin Harrison Jr.). They've concocted a plan to break the Hunger Games by blowing up the water tank that supplies the entire arena, flooding the computer systems and cutting off power to the entire operation. Haymitch succeeds initially, but the power is repaired quickly, Ampert is killed by woodland creatures swarming and gnawing his body to death, and as retaliation for the attack on the arena, Snow orders that the arena's volcano be activated.

Haymitch survives the eruption, and the deadly fire that engulfs the mountainous woods of the arena, but most of the surviving tributes do not (including fake-Louella, who died earlier by way of a poison pollen), leaving just five of them: Maysilee, a young girl named Wellie (Rada Rae), and two of the deadliest career tributes, Silka and Panache (Laura Marcus and Jhaleil Swaby).

It has been revealed that after a series of attacks, both by deadly birds and Silka and Panache, all of the other tributes have died, including Maysilee, but not before they promise each other to be the worst Hunger Games victor ever, should they emerge victorious. Haymitch is crowned as the victor of the Hunger Games, and he intends to stay true to his promise. But his battle is only just beginning, and it's about to get much worse.

Haymitch might have won the Hunger Games, but all of his actions in the arena are painted in a completely different light. His attack on the arena itself is not televised, and when he's presented to the Capitol as the winner in the recap hosted by Caesar Flickerman (Kieran Culkin), he's painted as a traitor and a coward, one who promised to help his fellow tributes against the careers but abandoned them as soon as the games started. Even the final kill of Silka, which happens after her thrown axe is deflected back at her by a shield protecting the power plant that gives energy to the arena, is mocked, as Haymitch couldn't even deliver the final blow himself to declare victory.

Industry observers note that things don't get better when he returns home, either. As soon as he arrives back in District 12, his mother and brother are killed in a house fire, clearly orchestrated by President Snow. But the final crushing blow comes when he reunites with Lenore. As they embrace, she eats what appears to be the gumdrops that he told his brother to give to Lenore before he left for the Hunger Games. But those aren't the same gumdrops. They're poisoned, courtesy of Snow, and Lenore dies in Haymitch's arms.

All of this pushes Haymitch to the brink, and he begins to drink heavily and isolate himself from the rest of District 12, even shunning the friendly Everdeen family, despite their efforts to help him work through the pain. He stays true to his word by becoming the worst Hunger Games victor, letting his tributes fail for years, refusing to participate in this barbaric entertainment. But there might yet be hope for Haymitch.

According to recent reports, why did President Snow let Haymitch live after defying the Capitol so clearly? In addition to being the victor of the Hunger Games, making it difficult for him to merely dispatch with him in the arena, Plutarch Heavensbee convinced Snow to reconsider killing Haymitch after the games were over. Knowing that their stunt to end the games didn't work, and the public was unable to see the tributes working together and sparking the rebellion in the districts needed to overthrow the Capitol, Heavensbee is pulling a move that feels reminiscent of Albus Dumbledore using Harry Potter to draw out Voldemort.

Plutarch is the one orchestrating the presentation of the Hunger Games to the public, and he knows what they need to see in order to sew a revolution properly. He's willing to turn Haymitch into an outcast and upend his life if it means there's even the smallest possibility that his defiance will eventually grow into the rebellion they need. He knows the continuation of the games will continue to create resentment, and they just need to wait for the right spark to emerge that will set fire to the hearts of every district in Panem. While it might feel like they've failed, this is still a small success that will lead to a future generation following in their footsteps.

Sources indicate that we already know how that story turns out, and "Sunrise on the Reaping" ends with Woody Harrelson returning as Haymitch Abernathy, admiring a memorial that now lies where the reaping once took place in District 12. He's joined by Katniss and Peeta Mellark (Josh Hutcherson), who wish him a happy birthday, allowing Haymitch to fulfill Lenore's dreams of keeping the sun from rising on another reaping. Haymitch paid dearly for decades, but the Hunger Games are finally over.

Steve Clarke didn’t crash and burn in the US because a raft of world-class talents failed to turn up on the biggest stage. It happened primarily because a limited squad was unable to outperform two top-ten nations in Brazil and Morocco who could call upon infinitely superior footballers.

Sebastian Pocognoli has since arrived on the scene having earned a stellar reputation from his title success with Union Saint-Gilloise and his less feted spell at Monaco. But he has not come armed with a magic wand.

In opening the door to a string of fresh faces and advocating the more attacking approach which so many craved, the turbulence he’s experienced to date should only have been expected.

Limited by both the standard of players who are eligible for Scotland and the time he has to work with them, only the blissfully naïve would have seen his appointment as a quick fix.

While there were some positives to be taken from the game with North Macedonia – primarily the result – it’s likely the nation will have to endure more short-term pain for long-term gain.

Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli greets his players after a satisfactory evening at Hampden.

This was always going to take time, perhaps, in the view of John McGinn, more than many may have imagined.

According to recent reports, ‘The manager’s got a great reputation, a good record at both places he’s been,’ said the Aston Villa captain. ‘The most crucial thing now in football is individuals don’t win you games. It’s unity, teamwork and everyone being on the same page.

‘You see how successful clubs and successful countries do it. And we want to be one of them.

It has been revealed that ‘It’s not going to happen overnight. There’s a lot to learn but we did create significant chances against North Macedonia where we could have scored three, four or five and it could be a different story.

Sources indicate that ‘But this isn’t something that gets fixed in March or even next September. It will start to build over the next 18 months.’.

If that predicted time frame might raise an eyebrow or two, McGinn makes no apology for it. Call it managing expectations from the midfielder if you please. But without a degree of patience from the Tartan Army, he feels Pocognoli’s ideas won’t take root.

‘I understand it’s frustrating,’ he added. ‘It’s freezing and you want to see four, five, six goals, but the balance has got to be there.

McGinn sends his penalty home to give Scotland a deserved lead against North Macedonia.

‘They’re entitled to their opinion, but there’s got to be a mixture of patience.

It has been revealed that ‘The supporters are entitled to say whatever they like. But just as long as they hurl anything they want to shout at the experienced boys and just let the young ones flourish and try and settle into the team.’.

In a recent development, give credit where it’s due. With Clarke accused of causing stagnation by selecting the same old faces, Pocognoli has capped five players for the first time while recalling the likes of Oli McBurnie.

In a recent development, the sages in the stands can’t have it both ways. If the squad was going to evolve, it was never going to be a smooth ride.

According to recent reports, ‘I think the young players are starting to show more now,’ McGinn stressed. ‘Luke Graham on Friday night, I thought he was brilliant. It’s not easy playing in the middle of a back three. He’s been waiting for his chance and the manager’s shown that if you deserve your chance you’re going to get put in there.

In a recent development, ‘We’ve got so many players that can step up and they will. We just need to show that belief and take it to the pitch.’.

Even in victory, McGinn doesn’t dispute that there is significant scope for improvement. He’s convinced, however, that this will all come good in the end.

McGinn insists it's vital the entire Scotland squad buy into the methods of manager Pocognoli.

In a recent development, ‘We need to play slightly better,’ he said. ‘We know that, but we’re going through a period which I’ve been used to at club level, a lot of changes, a lot of detail that we need to try and remember and get used to.

Recent findings suggest that ‘And it’s about sticking at it. We’re keen to play a style of football that’s not easy but is going to get bums off seats. It’s crucial that everyone believes in it because if one person drops off or doesn’t believe in it, that’s when it all starts to fall apart.’.

In a recent development, friday was another memorable night on a personal level for McGinn. Having broken the tension with the opener only to see North Macedonia level, he held his nerve to put Scotland back from the penalty spot.

In a recent development, the brace put him on 24 international goals, now within six of Denis Law and Kenny Dalglish. But all of that is for another day.

Industry observers note that ‘It feels a bit strange, but at the minute that’s gone to the back burner,’ he stressed. ‘I had a wee chat with Scott (McTominay) about the penalties. I was designated penalty taker but, to be fair, he’s not missed one I don’t think in his career.

McGinn is eyeing three points against Switzerland in St Gallen to close the campaign on a high.

Even if everything clicks for Pocognoli’s side, it will be the tallest of orders.

‘Difficult,’ stated McGinn. ‘I know they drew on Friday night (with Slovenia) but they’ve got a couple of players back that they were missing last time.

‘It is a tough one but we want to be competing against these teams away from home. It’s not going to be perfect for a while, but we’ll stick at it.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Patch, 8:41 p.m.: The Federal Aviation Administration announced it has ended the ground stop.

Industry observers note that on Friday afternoon, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ordered a nationwide ground stop for all airports in the United States. If you're planning to fly this afternoon or evening, or you have friends or family doing the same, you're likely concerned about tracking flight statuses. While there's still a lot we don't know, there are tools to help track flights at this time:.

There are a number of options for tracking flights, whether you have your flight number or not. If you have the flight number, the fastest method is to Google it: Google will display a live tracker of your flight at the top of the results page. You can also head to the airline's official website to track your flight: United Airlines, for example, has a flight tracker where you can either enter your route information or your flight number. Most, if not all, airlines will have a similar tool you can use.

It has been revealed that alternatively, you can use a site or service that tracks all flights. FlightAware is one such site and has a flight tracker that lets you search flights—so long as you know the origin and the destination. If you have the flight number, your iPhone can help: You can enter your flight number into Spotlight search to see a live tracker, or you can text a contact your flight number, then tap the link that appears under the number to see a tracker of the flight.

It has been revealed that at this time, the exact reason isn't totally clear. According to the agency, “The FAA issued a nationwide ground stop for all U.S. airports following communication issues impacting multiple Air Route Traffic Control Centers,” but the FAA hasn't said what caused those communications issues or when they expect to lift the grounding. The grounding order comes one day after a massive Microsoft outage that disrupted service for users of Outlook, Teams, and other Microsoft products. It also comes one day after Ars Technica reported that the FAA was rolling out an AI-powered tool to help manage air traffic across the country.

Sources indicate that this is only the third time in U.S. history that the FAA has made such an order—once after 9/11, and again in January of 2023 due to a pilot alert system issue; the latter ground stop lasted around 90 minutes.

32 Years Later, Mufasa's Best Lion King Line Is Still The Greatest Disney Quote Ever

💡 Key Takeaways
  • "The Lion King" is the crowning achievement of the Disney Renaissance.
  • It has been revealed that directed by Roger Allers and Rob Minkoff, "Lion King" was the highest grossing film of 1994 and, at the time, the second highest grossing film in history (earning more than $770 million during its initial release).
  • The 1998 sequel, "The Lion King II: Simba's Pride," is pretty good as far as direct-to-video Disney sequels go.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

"The Lion King" is the crowning achievement of the Disney Renaissance. If you were born after, say, 1989, then the movie was almost certainly a cornerstone of your childhood. That makes it amusing to look back and realize Disney didn't expect "The Lion King" to be one of the studio's greatest works.

It has been revealed that directed by Roger Allers and Rob Minkoff, "Lion King" was the highest grossing film of 1994 and, at the time, the second highest grossing film in history (earning more than $770 million during its initial release). More than any other animated Disney classic, "The Lion King" is a franchise unto itself — it's even been adapted as a Broadway play.

The 1998 sequel, "The Lion King II: Simba's Pride," is pretty good as far as direct-to-video Disney sequels go. Scene-stealing comic relief, and Simba's foster fathers, Timon & Pumbaa (Nathan Lane & Ernie Sabella, whose audition changed the movie), got their own TV show and spin-off movie "The Lion King 1 ½." Disney Jr. aired a sequel TV series, "The Lion Guard," and in 2019, Disney produced a photorealistic "Lion King" remake that got its own prequel, "Mufasa." Granted, that remake only proved how special the original and its luscious cartooning is.

An essential part of the majesty of "The Lion King" is the movie's sound. Hans Zimmer's Oscar-winning score, plus songs composed by Elton John with lyrics by Tim Rice. Even if you don't speak the Zulu language, who can't recall the opening "Circle of Life" song as all of the savannah marches to pride rock to pay tribute to new prince Simba (Jonathan Taylor Thomas)? Then there's the voice acting, especially the late James Earl Jones as Simba's father Mufasa — no voice in cinema history better feels like a real father and a king all at once.

Mufasa is murdered early on in "The Lion King" by his envious brother Scar (Jeremy Irons) staging a wildebeest stampede to trap Simba. (This complex sequence took three years to animate properly.) Simba, convinced by Scar it's all his fault, runs away in shame and spends years living in exile, learning "Hakuna Matata" (It means no worries!) from Timon and Pumbaa. When his childhood friend Nala (Moira Kelly) comes knocking, the grown Simba (Matthew Broderick) has to finally face his past.

With help from mandrill shaman Rafiki (Robert Guillaume), that's what Simba does. Mufasa once told Simba to look up into the sky to remember his father would always be with him. Mufasa literally manifests in the clouds, pushing Simba to fulfill his birthright: "Remember who you are. You are my son and the one true king.".

"The Lion King" is often called a kid-friendly staging of "Hamlet" with talking animals. This scene mirrors the ghost of Hamlet's murdered father talking to his son. But James Earl Jones' voice is so grand that it feels more like God speaking to Christ.

In a recent development, yet the scene also unfurls common criticism of "The Lion King" for its themes and political subtext. Textually, "The Lion King" is a pro-monarchy movie. It is quite literally about how the restoration of the proper heir to the throne heals the world. (The movie stacks the deck by making Scar a lazy and ill-equipped king on top of him being a kinslayer.) Mufasa frames Simba as the rightful king simply because he's the son of a king, suggesting (to quote Princess Azula of "Avatar: The Last Airbender") that "the divine right to rule is something you're born with." Pretty regressive attitude for the 1990s, but it's undeniably epic storytelling, too.

According to recent reports, "The Lion King" is filled with memorable quotes and song lyrics from its ensemble, so let's narrow that and list only Mufasa's greatest lines. Besides the inimitable power of James Earl Jones' voice, Mufasa's limited screentime — most of it spent schooling or bond with his son — makes every bit of his dialogue feels special.

When we think of Matt Damon, we picture the international film star, the public friendship with Ben Affleck, or even the Damon/Kimmel faux feud that started back in the early 2000s. We tend to forget that he has four daughters, which means countless family events, gatherings, birthdays, and shared experiences, and endless memories from when they were children. It was beyond heartwarming to see his reaction in real time as the father and daughter sharing time with Goofy brought him back to his own family.

In a recent development, he got called out on all of this in the interview because the host, Brittnee Blair, had recognized a similar look in her own husband watching their four-year-old daughter, knowing how fast time passes and that those moments will merely be memories. Being the movie star on a press tour that he is, the self-proclaimed “anti-Tom Cruise” also related it back to the movies of Christopher Nolan by saying:.

It’s a theme in a lot of Chris’ movies, right? Of a father missing the childhood of their kids. That video, one of my kids sent that to me. We were at Goofy’s Kitchen in Disneyland, and we’ve gone every year for my daughter’s birthday, and she was turning 18… And I had no idea somebody was recording that.

It has been revealed that I love when the timing lines up and someone can ask a celebrity to explain the story behind a viral moment, making them more relatable to everyone else. And there’s nothing more human than spending and missing time with our loved ones. I can’t imagine what the family in the video thought when they realized that not only was The Bourne Identity star at Disneyland on the same day, but he was in the background of their video, reacting to that special interaction.

There is no shortage of celebrity sightings at theme parks, from Disney super fan Charlize Theron to John Stamos, Adam Sandler, and so many others. Something like this moment with Matt Damon makes me not only want to keep an even more keen eye out, but also comb through my own videos for anyone making an unexpected cameo appearance in the background. Especially knowing that it could lead to another sweet backstory like this one.
